questions.q: If $\frac{x^2}{2 x^4+7 x^2+6}=\frac{A x+B}{x^2+a}+\frac{C x+D}{a x^2+3}$, then $A+B+C-2 D$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{x^2}{2 x^4+7 x^2+6}=\frac{x^2}{\left(x^2+2\right)\left(2 x^2+3\right)} \\ = & \frac{x^2+2-2}{\left(x^2+2\right)\left(2 x^2+3\right)}=\frac{1}{2 x^2+3}-\frac{2}{\left(x^2+2\right)\left(2 x^2+3\right)}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2 x^2+3}+2\left(\frac{1}{x^2+2}-\frac{2}{2 x^2+3}\right)=\frac{2}{x^2+2}-\frac{3}{2 x^2+3} \\ & a=2, A=0, C=0, B=2, D=-3 \\ & A+B+C-2 D=0+2+0-2 \times(-3)=8=4 a.\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $\int \frac{\sec x}{3(\sec x+\tan x)+2} d x=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & I=\int \frac{\sec x(\sec x-\tan x) d x}{3\left(\sec ^2 x-\tan ^2 x\right)+2(\sec x-\tan x)} \\ & \sec x-\tan x=t \\ & I=\int \frac{-d t}{3+2 t}=\frac{-1}{2} \ln (3+2 t)+C \\ &= \frac{-1}{2} \ln (3+2 \sec x-2 \tan x)+C \\ &= \frac{-1}{2} \ln \left(\frac{3 \cos x+2-2 \sin x}{\cos x}\right)+C \\ &= \frac{-1}{2} \ln \left[\frac{3-3 \tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}+2\left(1+\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}\right)-4 \tan \frac{x}{2}}{1-\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}}\right]+C \\ &= \frac{-1}{2} \ln \left[\frac{5-4 \tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}-\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}}{1-\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}}\right]+C\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2} \ln \left[\frac{1-\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}}{\left(1-\tan \frac{x}{2}\right)\left(5+\tan \frac{x}{2}\right)}\right]+C \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \ln \left(\frac{1+\tan \frac{x}{2}}{5+\tan \frac{x}{2}}\right)+C .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \frac{d x}{4+3 \cot x}=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & I=\int \frac{d x}{4+3 \cot x}=\int \frac{\sin x d x}{4 \sin x+3 \cos x} \\ &= \int \frac{A(4 \cos x-3 \sin x)+B(4 \sin x+3 \cos x)}{(4 \sin x+3 \cos x)} d x \\ &= \int\left[\frac{(4 B-3 A) \sin x+(3 B+4 A) \cos x}{4 \sin x+3 \cos x}\right] d x \\ & 3 B+4 A=0 \Rightarrow A=\frac{-3 B}{4} \\ & \Rightarrow 4 B-3 A=1 \Rightarrow 4 B+\frac{9 B}{4}=1 \Rightarrow B=\frac{4}{25} \Rightarrow A=\frac{-3}{25} \\ & I= \frac{-3}{25} \int \frac{(4 \cos x-3 \sin x) d x}{4 \sin x \cos x}+\int \frac{4}{25} d x+C \\ &= \frac{-3}{25} \ln |4 \sin x+3 \cos x|+\frac{4}{25} x+C.\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \frac{d x}{(x+1) \sqrt{x^2+4}}=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text{ Let } K=\int \frac{d x}{(x+1) \sqrt{x^2+4}} \\ & \text{ Let } x+1=\frac{1}{t} \Rightarrow x=\frac{1}{t}-1=\frac{1-t}{t} \Rightarrow d x=-\frac{1}{t^2} d t \\ & I=-\int \frac{\frac{1}{t^2} d t}{\frac{1}{t} \sqrt{\left(\frac{1-t}{t}\right)^2+4}}=-\int \frac{\sqrt{t^2} d t}{t \sqrt{(1-t)^2+4 t^2}} \\ & =-\int \frac{d t}{\sqrt{\left(1-t^2\right)+4 t^2}}=-\int \frac{d t}{\sqrt{5 t^2-2 t+1}} \times \frac{\frac{\sqrt{5}}{\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}}}{2} \\ & =\frac{-\sqrt{5}}{2} \int \frac{d t}{\sqrt{\frac{25}{4} t^2-\frac{5}{2} t+\frac{5}{4}}}=\frac{-\sqrt{5}}{2} \int \frac{d t}{\sqrt{\frac{25}{4}} t^2+\frac{1}{4}-\frac{5}{2} t+1} \\ & =\frac{-\sqrt{5}}{2} \int \frac{d t}{\sqrt{\left(\frac{5}{2} t-\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+1}} \\ & =\frac{-\sqrt{5}}{2} \times \frac{2}{5} \sinh ^{-1}\left(\frac{5 t}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\right)+C\left[\because \int \frac{d t}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}=\sinh ^{-1} x\right] \\ & I=\frac{-1}{\sqrt{5}} \sinh ^{-1}\left(\frac{5 t-1}{2}\right)+C \text{ Put } t=\frac{1}{x+1}\end{aligned}I=\frac{-1}{\sqrt{5}} \sinh ^{-1}\left(\frac{\frac{5}{x+1}-1}{2}\right)+C=\frac{-1}{\sqrt{5}} \sinh ^{-1}\left(\frac{4-x}{2(x+1)}\right)+C$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int e^x\left(x^3+x^2-x+4\right) d x=e^x f(x)+c$, then $f(1)=$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \int e^x\left(x^3+x^2-x+4\right) d x=e^x f(x)+\mathrm{c} \\
\Rightarrow & e^x\left(x^3+x^2-x+4\right)=e^x f^{\prime}(x)+e^x f(x) \\
\Rightarrow & f(x)+f^{\prime}(x)=x^3+x^2-x+4
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \text{ Let } f(x)=x^3+a x^2+b x+c \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x)=3 x^2+2 a x+b \\
& \Rightarrow x^3+x^2-x+4=x^3+(a+3) x^2+(2 a+b) x+b+c \\
& \Rightarrow a+3=1 \Rightarrow a=-2 \Rightarrow 2 a+b=-1 \Rightarrow b=3 \\
& b+c=4 \Rightarrow c=1 \therefore f(x)=x^3-2 x^2+3 x+1 \\
& f(1)=1-2+3+1=3
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\frac{1}{x^4+x^2+1}=\frac{A x+B}{x^2+a x+1}+\frac{C x+D}{x^2-a x+1}$ then $A+B-C+D=$
questions.solution:
$\frac{1}{x^4+x^2+1}=\frac{A x+B}{x^2+a x+1}+\frac{C x+D}{x^2-a x+1}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathbb{1}=(\mathrm{A} x+\mathrm{B})\left(x^2-a x+1\right)+(\mathrm{C} x+\mathrm{D})\left(x^2+a x+1\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \mathbb{1}=\mathrm{A}\left(x^3-a x^2+x\right)+\mathrm{B}\left(x^2-a x+1\right)+\mathrm{C}\left(x^3+a x^2+x\right)+\end{aligned}D\left(x^2+a x+1\right)\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 1=(\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{C}) x^3+(-a \mathrm{ A}+\mathrm{B}+\mathrm{C} a+\mathrm{D}) x^2+(\mathrm{A}-a \mathrm{ B}+\mathrm{C} \\ & +a \mathrm{D}) x+\mathbb{B}+\mathbb{D}\end{aligned}$
On comparing
$A+C=0$..(i)
$-a \mathrm{ A}+\mathrm{B}+\mathrm{Ca}+\mathrm{D}=0$...(ii)
$\mathrm{A}-a \mathrm{ B}+\mathrm{C}+a \mathrm{D}=0$...(iii)
$B+D=1$...(iv)
From (i), (iii)
$-a \mathrm{ B}+a \mathrm{D}=0$...(v)
From (iv) and (v) $; 2 a \mathrm{D}=a \Rightarrow \mathrm{D}=\frac{1}{2} and \mathrm{B}=\frac{1}{2}$ From (iii) and (iv)
$-a \mathrm{ A}+a \mathrm{C}=-1$..(vi)
From (i) and (vi) $; 2 a \mathrm{C}=-1 ; \mathrm{C}=\frac{-1}{2 a}, \mathrm{ A}=\frac{-1}{2 a}\therefore \mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{D}=\frac{1}{2 a}+\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2 a}+\frac{1}{2}=1+\frac{1}{a}$
Now, comparing the denominator
$\begin{aligned} & x^4+x^2+1=\left(x^2-a x+1\right)\left(x^2+a x+1\right) \\ & =x^4+a x^3+x^2-a x^3-a^2 x^2-a x+x^2+a x+1 \\ & =x^4+\left(2-a^2\right) x^2+1\end{aligned}$
On comparing $x^2$ term
$\begin{aligned} & 2-a^2=1 \Rightarrow a^2=1 \Rightarrow a=1 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{ A}+\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{D}=1+\frac{1}{a}=1+1=2=2 a\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
If $\int \frac{1}{x^4+8 x^2+9} d x=\frac{1}{k}\left[\frac{1}{\sqrt{14}} \tan ^{-1}(f(x))-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \tan ^{-1}(g(x))\right]+c$,
then $\sqrt{\frac{k}{2}+f(\sqrt{3})+g(1)}=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{1}{x^4+8 x^2+9} d x=\int \frac{\frac{1}{x^2}}{x^2+8+\frac{9}{x^2}} d x \\ & =\frac{1}{6} \int \frac{\left(1+\frac{3}{x^2}\right)}{\left(x-\frac{3}{x}\right)^2+14} d x-\frac{1}{6} \int \frac{\left(1-\frac{3}{x^2}\right)}{\left(x+\frac{3}{x}\right)^2+2} d x \\ & \text{ Let }x-\frac{3}{x}=t \text{$ and $} x+\frac{3}{x}=\frac{1}{6} \int \frac{d t}{t^2+(\sqrt{14})^2}-\frac{1}{6} \int \frac{d(\mu}{\mu^2+(\sqrt{2})^2} \\ & \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{6}\left[\frac{1}{\sqrt{14}} \tan ^{-1} \frac{t}{\sqrt{14}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \tan ^{-1} \frac{\mu}{\sqrt{2}}\right]+c \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}=6, \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\frac{1}{\sqrt{14}}\left(x-\frac{3}{x}\right), g(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(x+\frac{3}{x}\right)\end{aligned}\therefore \sqrt{\frac{k}{2}+f(\sqrt{3})+g(1)}=\sqrt{3+2 \sqrt{2}}=(\sqrt{1+\sqrt{2}})^2=\sqrt{2}+1$

questions.q: $\int \frac{1}{x^m \sqrt[m]{x^m+1}} d x=$
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{I}=\int \frac{1}{x^m\left(x^m+\right)^{\frac{1}{m}}} d x$ Let $u=\mathrmx^{1-\mathrm{m}} ; d u=\frac{1-m}{x^m} d xx^m=u^{\frac{m}{1-m}}\mathrm{I}=-\frac{1}{m-1} \int \frac{d u}{\left(u^{\frac{m}{1-m}})+1\right)^{\frac{1}{m}}}=\frac{-1}{m-1} \int \frac{u^{\frac{1}{m-1}}}{\left(u^{\frac{m}{m-1}}+1\right)^{\frac{1}{m}}} d u$
Let $u^{\frac{m}{m-1}}+1=v \Rightarrow d v=mu^\frac{{\frac{m}{m-1}}-1}{m-1}-d u$
$\mathbb{I}=\frac{-1}{m} \int \frac{1}{v^{\frac{1}{m}}} d v \Rightarrow \mathbb{I}=\frac{-v^{1-\frac{1}{m}}}{(1-\frac{1}{m})m}\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}=\frac{\left(u^{\frac{m}{m-1}}+1\right)^{1-\frac{1}{m}}}{\left(1-\frac{1}{m}\right)^m}+\mathrm{C} ; \mathrm{I}=\frac{-\left(x^{\frac{(1-m) m}{m-1}}+1\right)^{\mathfrak{1}-\frac{1}{m}}}{\left(1-\frac{1}{m}\right) m}+\mathrm{C} \\ & \mathrm{I}=\frac{-1}{m-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt[m]{x^m+1}}{x}\right)^{m-1}+\mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\int\left(1+x-x^{-1}\right) e^{x+x^{-1}} d x=f(x)+c$, then $f(1)-f(-1)=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}=\int\left(1+x-\frac{1}{x}\right) e^{x+\frac{1}{x}} d x \\ & =\int e^{\left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right)} d x+\int x\left(1-\frac{1}{x^2}\right) e^{\left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right)} d x \\ & \text{ Using } \int\left[f(x)+x f^{\prime}(x)\right] d x=x f(x)+c \\ & \mathbb{I}=x e^{\left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right)}+c \\ & f(1)-f(-1)=e^2+\frac{1}{e^2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int(\sqrt{\operatorname{cosec} x+1}) d x=k \tan ^{-1}(f(x))+c$, then $\frac{1}{k} f\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}=\int \sqrt{\operatorname{cosec} x+1} d x \\ = & \int \sqrt{\frac{\tan ^2\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)+1}{2 \tan \left(\frac{x}{2}\right)}+1} d x\end{aligned}\operatorname{Let} u=\tan \frac{x}{2} \Rightarrow d x=\frac{2}{u^2+1} d u\begin{aligned} \mathbb{I} & =\sqrt{2} \int \frac{\sqrt{\frac{u^2+\mathbb{1}}{u}+2}}{u^2+1} d u \\ & =\sqrt{2} \int \frac{u+1}{\sqrt{u}\left(u^2+1\right)} d u\end{aligned}$
Let $v=\sqrt{u} \Rightarrow d v=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{u}}\begin{aligned} I & =2 \sqrt{2} \int \frac{v^2+1}{v^4+1} d v \\ & =2 \sqrt{2} \int \frac{v^2+1}{\left(v^2-\sqrt{2} v+1\right)\left(v^2+\sqrt{2} v+1\right)} d v \\ & =\sqrt{2} \int \frac{1}{v^2+\sqrt{2} v+1} d v+\sqrt{2} \int \frac{1}{v^2-\sqrt{2} v+1} d v \\ & =\sqrt{2} \int \frac{1}{\left(v+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2+\frac{1}{2}} d v+\sqrt{2} \int \frac{1}{\left(v-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2+\frac{1}{2}} d v\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =2 \tan ^{-1}(\sqrt{2} v+1)+2 \tan ^{-1}(\sqrt{2} v-1) \\ & =2 \tan ^{-1}(\sqrt{2} u+1)+2 \tan ^{-1}(\sqrt{2} u-1)\end{aligned}=2 \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2} u}{1-u}\right)=2 \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2 \tan \frac{x}{2}}}{1-\tan \frac{x}{2}}\right)\Rightarrow k=2, f(x)=\frac{\sqrt{2 \tan \frac{x}{2}}}{1-\tan \frac{x}{2}} \quad\left[\because \tan \frac{\pi}{12}=2-\sqrt{3}\right]\Rightarrow \frac{1}{k} f\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{1}{2} \frac{\sqrt{4-2 \sqrt{3}}}{1-(2-\sqrt{3})}=\frac{1}{2} \frac{\sqrt{(1-\sqrt{3})^2}}{\sqrt{3}-1}=\frac{-1}{2}$

questions.q: $\int \sqrt{4 \cos ^2 x-5 \sin ^2 x} \cos x d x=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & I=\int \sqrt{4 \cos ^2 x-5 \sin ^2 x} \cos x d x \\ & =\int \sqrt{4-9 \sin ^2 x} \cos x d x ; \text{ Let } \sin x=\frac{2}{3} t \Rightarrow d x=\frac{2 d t}{3 \cos x} \\ & I=\int \frac{4}{3} \sqrt{1-t^2} d t \Rightarrow I=\frac{4}{3}\left[\frac{t}{2} \sqrt{1-t^2}+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1} t\right]+C \\ & \Rightarrow I=\frac{4}{3}\left[\frac{3}{4} \sin x \sqrt{1-\frac{9}{4} \sin ^2 x}+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{2} \sin x\right)\right]+C \\ & \Rightarrow I=\frac{1}{2} \sin x \sqrt{4-9 \sin ^2 x}+\frac{2}{3} \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{3 \sin x}{2}\right)+C\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int\left(\frac{4 \tan ^4 x+3 \tan ^2 x-1}{\tan ^2 x+4}\right) d x=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \quad I=\int \frac{4 \tan ^4 x+3 \tan ^2 x-1}{\tan ^2 x+4} d x \\ & I=\int \frac{\left(4 \tan ^2 x-1\right)\left(\tan ^2 x+1\right)}{\tan ^2 x+4} d x \\ & I=\int \frac{\sec ^2 x(2 \tan x-1)(2 \tan x+1)}{\tan ^2 x+4} d x \\ & \text{ Let } \tan x=u \Rightarrow \sec ^2 x d x=d u \\ & \Rightarrow I=\int \frac{(2 u-1)(2 u+1)}{u^2+4} d u=\int \frac{4\left(u^2+4\right)-17}{\left(u^2+4\right)} d u \\ & \Rightarrow I=\int\left(4-\frac{17}{u^2+4}\right) d u=4 \int d u-17 \int \frac{d u}{u^2+4} \\ & \Rightarrow I=4 u-\frac{17}{2} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{u}{2}\right)+C \\ & \Rightarrow I=4 \tan x-\frac{17}{2} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\tan x}{2}\right)+C\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: $\int x^3 \sin 3 x d x=x^3\left(\frac{-\cos 3 x}{3}\right)+\int x^2 \cos 3 x d x\begin{aligned} & =-x^3 \frac{\cos 3 x}{3}+x^2 \frac{\sin 3 x}{3}-\frac{2}{3} \int(x \sin 3 x) d x \\ & =-x^3 \frac{\cos 3 x}{3}+\frac{x^2 \sin 3 x}{3}-\frac{2}{3}\left[\frac{-x \cos 3 x}{3}+\int \frac{\cos 3 x}{3} d x\right] \\ & =-x^3 \frac{\cos 3 x}{3}+x^2 \frac{\sin 3 x}{3}+2 x \frac{\cos 3 x}{9}-\frac{2}{27} \sin 3 x \\ & =\cos 3 x\left\{\frac{-x^3}{3}+\frac{2 x}{9}\right\}+\sin 3 x\left(\frac{x^2}{3}-\frac{2}{27}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow f(x)=\frac{-x^3}{3}+\frac{2 x}{9} ; g(x)=\frac{x^2}{3}-\frac{2}{27} \\ & \Rightarrow 27 \cdot\left(\frac{-x^3}{3}+\frac{2 x}{9}+\frac{x^3}{3}-\frac{2 x}{27}\right)=27 \times \frac{4 x}{27}=4 x\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $\int(\sqrt{1-\sin x}+\sqrt{1+\sin x}) \mathrm{dx}=f(x)+c$, where $c$ is the constant of integration. If $\frac{5 \pi}{2} < x < \frac{7 \pi}{2}$ and $f\left(\frac{8 \pi}{3}\right)=-2$, then $f^{\prime}\left(\frac{8 \pi}{3}\right)=$
questions.solution: $\mathrm{I}=\int(\sqrt{1-\sin \mathrm{x}}+\sqrt{1+\sin \mathrm{x}}) \mathrm{dx}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow I=\int\left(\sqrt{1-\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}+\sqrt{1+\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}\right) d x \\ & \left.\Rightarrow I=\sqrt{2} \int\left[\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{x}{2}\right)\right] x+\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{x}{2}\right)\right] d x \\ & \Rightarrow I=2 \sqrt{2} \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{x}{2}\right)-2 \sqrt{2} \sin \left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{x}{2}\right)+C\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =4 \cos \left(\frac{x}{2}\right)+C \Rightarrow f(x)=4 \cos \left(\frac{x}{2}\right) \Rightarrow f\left(\frac{8 \pi}{3}\right)=-2 \\ & \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x)=-2 \sin \frac{x}{2} \Rightarrow f^{\prime}\left(\frac{8 \pi}{3}\right)=\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: Let $x^2=8 \Rightarrow 2 x d x=d t\begin{aligned} & I=\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{\left(t^2+1\right) d t}{\left(t^4+1\right)}=\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{\left(1+\frac{1}{t^2}\right) d t}{\left(t^2+\frac{1}{t^2}\right)} \\ & \Rightarrow L e t t-\frac{1}{t}=u \Rightarrow\left(1+\frac{1}{t^2}\right) d t=d u \\ & \mathbb{I}=\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{d u}{u^2+2}=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{2}} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{u}{\sqrt{2}}\right)+c \\ & =\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{2}} \tan ^{-1}\left\{\left(t-\frac{1}{t}\right) \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right\}+c \\ & =\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{2}} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{x^4-1}{\sqrt{2} x^2}\right)+c\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $f(x)=\int \frac{\sin 2 x+2 \cos x}{4 \sin ^2 x+5 \sin x+1} d x$ and $f(0)=0$, then $f\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=$
questions.solution: $\int \frac{(2 \sin x \cos x+2 \cos x) d x}{4 \sin ^2 x+4 \sin x+\sin x+1}\begin{aligned} & =\int \frac{2(1+\sin x) \cos x d x}{(\sin x+1)(4 \sin x+1)} \\ & f(x)=\int \frac{2 \cos x}{4 \sin x+1}-d x=\frac{1}{2} \ln |4 \sin x+1|+c \\ & f(0)=0=\frac{1}{2} \ln (x)=0 \\ & f(x)=\frac{1}{2} \ln |4 \sin x+1| \Rightarrow f\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{1}{2} \ln 3.\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $\int \frac{1+\sqrt{3} \cot x}{1-\sqrt{3} \cot x} d x=$
questions.solution:
ac{\tan x+\sqrt{3}}{\tan x-\sqrt{3}} d x\begin{aligned} & =\int \frac{\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}+\sqrt{3}}{\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}-\sqrt{3}} d x=\int \frac{\sin x+\sqrt{3} \cos x}{\sin x-\sqrt{3} \cos x} d x \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \sin x+\sqrt{3} \cos x=K_1 \cdot \frac{d}{d x}(\sin x-\sqrt{3} \cos x) \\ & \quad+K_2(\sin x-\sqrt{3} \cos x) \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \sin x+\sqrt{3} \cos x=K_1(\cos x+\sqrt{3} \sin x) \\ & \quad+K_2(\sin x-\sqrt{3} \cos x) \\ & =\left(\sqrt{3} K_1+K_2\right) \sin x+\left(K_1-\sqrt{3} K_2\right) \cos x\end{aligned}\therefore \quad \sqrt{3} K_1+K_2=1$ ...(i)
$K_1-\sqrt{3} K_2=\sqrt{3}$ ...(ii)
$\therefore \quad K_1=\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{3} K_2$
From (i), $\sqrt{3}\left(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{3} K_2\right)+K_2=1\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad 3+4 K_2=1 \Rightarrow K_2=\frac{-1}{2} \\ & \therefore \quad K_1=\sqrt{3}\left(1+K_2\right)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ & \therefore \quad \int \frac{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}(\cos x+\sqrt{3} \sin x)-\frac{1}{2}(\sin x-\sqrt{3} \cos x)}{(\sin x-\sqrt{3} \cos x)} d x \\ & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \int \frac{\cos x+\sqrt{3} \sin x}{\sin x-\sqrt{3} \cos x} d x-\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{\sin x-\sqrt{3} \cos x}{\sin x-\sqrt{3} \cos x} d x \\ & =\frac{-1}{2} x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \ln |\sin x-\sqrt{3} \cos x|+C \\ & =\frac{-1}{2} x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \ln 2\left|\frac{1}{2} \sin x-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cos x\right|+C \\ & =\frac{-1}{2} x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \ln 2\left|\sin \left(x-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right|+C \\ & =\frac{-1}{2} x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \ln \left|\sin \left(x-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right|+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \ln 2+C \\ & =\frac{-1}{2} x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \ln \left|\sin \left(x-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right|+C\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $\begin{aligned} & \text{ If } \int \frac{1}{\operatorname{cosec} x+\cos x} d x=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{3}} \log |f(x)| \\ & -\int \frac{\cos x-\sin x}{2+\sin 2 x} d x+c \text{ then at } x=\frac{\pi}{3},|f(x)|=\end{aligned}$
questions.solution:
$\int \frac{1}{\operatorname{cosec} x+\cos x} d x\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{3}} \log \mid f(x) 1-\int \frac{\cos x-\sin x}{2+\sin 2 x} d x+C \\ & \Rightarrow \int \frac{d x}{\frac{1}{\sin x}+\cos x} \\ & =\int \frac{\sin x d x}{1+\sin x \cdot \cos x}=\int \frac{2 \sin x}{2+\sin 2 x} d x \\ & =\int \frac{\sin x+\cos x+\sin x-\cos x}{2+\sin 2 x} d x \\ & =\int \frac{\sin x+\cos x}{2+\sin 2 x}-\int \frac{\cos x-\sin x}{2+\sin 2 x} d x \\ & \therefore \quad \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{3}} \log |f(x)|=\int \frac{\sin x+\cos x}{2+\sin 2 x} d x \\ & I=\int \frac{\sin x+\cos x}{2+\sin 2 x} d x \\ & =\int \frac{\sin x+\cos x}{3-\sin ^2 x-\cos ^2 x+2 \sin x \cos x} d x\end{aligned}=\int \frac{\sin x+\cos x}{3-(\sin x-\cos x)^2} d x$
Let, $\sin x-\cos x=t,(\cos x+\sin x) d x=d t\begin{aligned} & \int \frac{d t}{3-t^2}=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{3}} \log \left|\frac{\sqrt{3}+t}{\sqrt{3}-t}\right|+C \\ & =\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{3}} \log \left|\frac{\sqrt{3}+\sin x-\cos x}{\sqrt{3}-\sin x+\cos x}\right|+C \\ & \therefore \quad f(x)=\frac{\sqrt{3}+\sin x-\cos x}{\sqrt{3}-\sin x+\cos x} \\ & \text{ at } x=\frac{\pi}{3} \\ & \therefore \quad f(x)=\frac{\sqrt{3}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}}{\sqrt{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{3 \sqrt{3}-1}{\sqrt{3}+1}.\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int(\log x)^3 x^5 d x=\frac{x^6}{A}\left[B(\log x)^3+C(\log x)^2+\right.\mathrm{D}(\operatorname{lug} \mathrm{x})-1]+\mathrm{k}$ and $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}, \mathrm{D}$ are integers, then $A-(B+C+D)=$
questions.solution: $\int(\log x)^3 x_{\text{II }^5 d x\begin{aligned} & =(\log x)^3 \cdot \int x^5 d x-\int\left(\frac{d}{d x}(\log x)^3\right) \cdot\left(\int x^5 d x\right) d x \\ & =\frac{x^6}{6}(\log x)^3-\int\left(\frac{3(\log x)^2}{x} \cdot \frac{x^6}{6}\right) d x\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{x^6}{6}(\log x)^3-\frac{1}{2} \int(\log x)^2 x^5 d x \\ & =\frac{x^6}{6}(\log x)^3-\frac{1}{2}\left[(\log x)^2 \cdot \frac{x^6}{6}-\int 2 \frac{\log x}{x} \cdot \frac{x^6}{6} d x\right] \\ & =\frac{x^6}{6}(\log x)^3-\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{x^6}{6}(\log x)^2-\frac{1}{3} \int \log x \cdot x_{\text{II }^5 d x\right] \\ & =\frac{x^6}{6}\left[(\log x)^3-\frac{1}{2}(\log x)^2\right]+\frac{1}{6}\left[\frac{x^6}{6} \cdot \log x-\int \frac{1}{x} \cdot \frac{x^6}{6} d x\right] \\ & =\frac{x^6}{6}\left[(\log x)^3-\frac{1}{2}(\log x)^2+\frac{1}{6} \log x\right]-\frac{1}{6 \times 6} \int x^5 d x \\ & =\frac{x^6}{6}\left[(\log x)^3-\frac{1}{2}(\log x)^2+\frac{1}{6} \log x-\frac{1}{36}\right]+k \\ & =\frac{x^6}{6}\left[\frac{36(\log x)^3-18(\log x)^2+6(\log x)-1}{36}\right]+k\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{x^6}{216}\left[36(\log x)^3-18(\log x)^2+6(\log x)-1\right]+k \\ & A=216, B=36, C=-18, D=6 \\ & A-(B+C+D) \\ & =216-(36-18+6)=192\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\int \frac{2 \sin 2 x-3 \cos x}{2 \sin ^2 x-3 \sin x+4} d x=f(x)+c$ where $c$ is the constant of integration, then $f\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)-f(0)=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int \frac{2 \sin 2 x-3 \cos x}{2 \sin ^2 x-3 \sin x+4} d x=\int \frac{\cos x(4 \sin x-3)}{2 \sin ^2 x-3 \sin x+4} d x \\ & \text{ Let } \sin x=t, \cos x d x=d t=\int \frac{(4 t-3)}{2 t^2-3 t+4} d t \\ & 2 t^2-3 t+4=u \Rightarrow(4 t-3) d t=d u \\ & \therefore \quad \int \frac{d u}{u}=\ln |u|+C=\ln \left|^{2} t^2-3 t+4\right|+C \\ & \quad=\ln \left(2 \sin ^2 x-3 \sin x+4\right)+C \\ & \therefore \quad f(x)=\ln \left(2 \sin ^2 x-3 \sin x+4\right) \\ & f\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)-f(0)=\ln 3-\ln 4=\ln \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)=\log \left(\frac{3}{4}\right).\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int(\sqrt{1-\sin x}+\sqrt{1+\sin x}) d x \\ & \because \frac{3 \pi}{2} < x < \frac{5 \pi}{2} \Rightarrow \frac{3 \pi}{4} < \frac{x}{2} < \frac{5 \pi}{4} \\ & \because \ln \left(\frac{3 \pi}{4}, \frac{5 \pi}{4}\right), \sin \frac{x}{2} > \cos \frac{x}{2} \\ = & \int\left(\sqrt{\left(\cos \frac{x}{2}-\sin \frac{x}{2}\right)^2}+\sqrt{\left(\cos \frac{x}{2}+\sin \frac{x}{2}\right)^2}\right) d x \\ = & \left.\int\left(\left|\cos \frac{x}{2}-\sin \frac{x}{2}\right|+\cos \frac{x}{2}+\sin \frac{x}{2}\right)\right) d x \\ = & \int\left(\sin \frac{x}{2}-\cos \frac{x}{2}+\sin \frac{x}{2}+\cos \frac{x}{2}\right) d x \\ = & 2 \int \sin \frac{x}{2} d x=2 \times 2\left[-\cos \frac{x}{2}\right]+C \\ = & -4 \cos \frac{x}{2}+C \Rightarrow f(x)=-4 \cos \frac{x}{2} \\ \therefore & f\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)-f(0)=-4 \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)+4 \cos 0=4-\frac{4 \sqrt{3}}{2} .\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int \frac{2 x+3}{\sqrt{3 x^2-2 x+1}} d x=\frac{1}{3} \int \frac{6 x-2+\frac{11}{3}}{\sqrt{3 x^2-2 x+1}} d x \\ & =\frac{1}{3}\left[\int \frac{(6 x-2) d x}{\sqrt{3 x^2-2 x+1}}+\frac{11}{3} \int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{3 x^2-2 x+1}}\right] \\ & I_1=\int \frac{6 x-2}{\sqrt{3 x^2-2 x+1}} d x \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt{3 x^2-2 x+1}=t\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{(6 x-2) d x}{2 \sqrt{3 x^2-2 x+1}}=d t \\ & \therefore \quad \int 2 d t=2 t+C=2 \sqrt{3 x^2-2 x+1}+C \\ & I_2=\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{3 x^2-2 x+1}}=\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{3\left(x^2-\frac{2}{3} x+\frac{1}{3}\right)}} \\ & =\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{3}\left[\left(x-\frac{1}{3}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\right)^2\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}} \\ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \times \frac{3}{\sqrt{2}} \sin h^{-1}\left(\frac{x-\frac{1}{3}}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2+C \\ & I_2=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}} \sin h^{-1}\left(\frac{3 x-1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)+C \\ & \therefore \quad I=\frac{2}{3} \sqrt{3 x^2-2 x+1}+\frac{11}{9} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}} \sin h^{-1}\left(\frac{3 x-1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)+C . \\ & =\frac{2}{3} \sqrt{3 x^2-2 x+1}+\frac{11}{3 \sqrt{6}} \sin h^{-1}\left(\frac{3 x-1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)+C\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \frac{1}{(x-2)\left(x^2+1\right)} d x=$
questions.solution: $\int \frac{d x}{(x-2)\left(x^2+1\right)}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{(x-2)\left(x^2+1\right)}=\frac{A}{x-2}+\frac{B x+C}{x^2+1} \\ & \Rightarrow 1=A\left(x^2+1\right)+(B x+C)(x-2) \\ & \text{ Put } x=2 \\ & \Rightarrow 1=5 A \Rightarrow A=\frac{1}{5} \\ & \Rightarrow 1=(A+B) x^2+(C-2 B) x+(A-2 C) \\ & \Rightarrow A+B=0 \Rightarrow B=-A=\frac{-1}{5} \\ & \Rightarrow C-2 B=0 \Rightarrow C=2 B=\frac{-2}{5} \\ & \therefore \int \frac{d x}{(x-2)\left(x^2+1\right)}=\int \frac{d x}{5(x-2)}+\int \frac{\frac{-1}{5} x-\frac{2}{5}}{x^2+1} d x \\ & =\frac{1}{5} \int \frac{d x}{x-2}-\frac{1}{5} \int \frac{x+2}{x^2+1} d x \\ & =\frac{1}{5} \log |x-2|-\frac{1}{5}\left[\int \frac{x d x}{x^2+1}+\int \frac{2 d x}{x^2+1}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{5}\left[\log |x-2|-\frac{1}{2} \log \left(x^2+1\right)-2 \tan ^{-1} x\right]+C \\ & =\frac{1}{5}\left[\log \frac{|x-2|}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}-2 \tan ^{-1} x\right]+C \\ & \end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\frac{x^4}{(x-1)(x-2)(x-3)}=p(x)+\frac{A}{x-1}+\frac{B}{x-2}+\frac{C}{x-3}$ then $p\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)+\mathrm{C}=$
questions.solution:
$\frac{x^4}{(x-1)(x-2)(x-3)}=P(x)+\frac{A}{x-1}+\frac{B}{x-2}+\frac{C}{x-3}$.
$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad x^4=P(x) \cdot(x-1) & (x-2)(x-3)+A(x-2)(x-3) \\ & +B(x-1)(x-3)+C(x-1)(x-2)\end{aligned}$
Put $x=1\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad 1=A(1-2)(1-3) \Rightarrow A=\frac{1}{2} \\
& \text{ Put } x=2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 16=B(2-1)(2-3) \Rightarrow B=-16
\end{aligned}$
Put $x=2\Rightarrow 16=B(2-1)(2-3) \Rightarrow B=-16$
Put $x=3\Rightarrow 81=C(3-1)(3-2) \Rightarrow C=\frac{81}{2}$
Putting $x=\frac{3}{2}$.
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^4=\left\{P\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)\right\}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(\frac{-1}{2}\right)\left(\frac{-3}{2}\right)+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(\frac{-1}{2}\right)\left(\frac{-3}{2}\right) \\
& +(-16)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(\frac{-3}{2}\right)+\left(\frac{81}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{-1}{2}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{81}{16}=\frac{3}{8} \cdot P\left\{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)\right\}+\frac{3}{8}+\frac{48}{4}-\frac{81}{8} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{3}{8} \cdot P\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)=\frac{81}{16}-\frac{3}{8}-\frac{48}{4}+\frac{81}{8} \Rightarrow P\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)=\frac{15}{2} \\
& \therefore \quad P\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)+C=\frac{15}{2}+\frac{81}{2}=\frac{96}{2}=48 .
\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} & I_n=\int \frac{\sin n x}{\sin x} d x=\int \frac{\sin [(n-1) x+x]}{\sin x} d x \\ = & \int \frac{\sin (n-1) x \cos x d x}{\sin x}+\int \frac{(\cos (n-1) x) \cdot(\sin x)}{\sin x} d x \\ = & \frac{1}{2} \int \frac{2 \sin (n-1) x \cdot \cos x}{\sin x} \frac{d x}{x}+\int \cos (n-1) x d x \\ = & \frac{1}{2} \int \frac{\sin n x+\sin (n-2)}{\sin x} d x+\frac{\sin (n-1)}{(n-1)} \\ & I_n=\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{\sin n x}{\sin x} d x+\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{\sin (n-2)}{\sin x} d x+\frac{\sin (n-1) x}{(n-1)} \\ & I_n=\frac{1}{2} I_n+\frac{1}{2} I_{n-2}+\frac{\sin (n-1) x}{(n-1)} \\ \Rightarrow & I_n-I_{n-2}=\frac{2 \sin (n-1) x}{n-1}\end{aligned}$
Put $n=n+1\Rightarrow \quad I_{n+1}-I_{n-1}=\frac{2 \sin n x}{n}$

$⇒ x^{2} - 3x + 2 = A\left(x^{2} + 9 - 6x\right) + B\left(x^{2} - 7x + 12\right) + ( Cx - 4C )$

So,

$A + B = 1 . . . \left(1\right)$

$- 6A - 7B + C = - 3 . . . \left(2\right)$

questions.solution:
Given:

$f\left(x\right) = ∫ \left(\dfrac{2x^{3} - 3x^{2} + 4x - 5}{x2}\right)dx$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = ∫ \left(2x - 3 + \dfrac{4}{x} - \dfrac{5}{x2}\right)dx$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = x^{2} - 3x + 4logx + \dfrac{5}{x} + C$

where, $C$ is the constant of integartion.

$f\left(1\right) = 1$

$⇒ 1 - 3 + 4 \times 0 + 5 + C = 1$

$⇒ C = - 2$

So,

$f\left(x\right) = x^{2} - 3x + 4logx + \dfrac{5}{x} - 2$

$⇒ f\left(5\right) = 25 - 15 + 4log5 + 1 - 2$

$⇒ f\left(5\right) = 9 + 4log5$

questions.solution:
Given:

$\dfrac{{x}^{2} + 3}{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)\left({x}^{2} + 2\right)} = \dfrac{Ax + B}{{x}^{2} + 1} + \dfrac{Cx + D}{{x}^{2} + 2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{x}^{2} + 3}{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)\left({x}^{2} + 2\right)} = \dfrac{\left(Ax + B\right)\left({x}^{2} + 2\right) + \left(Cx + D\right)\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)}{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)\left({x}^{2} + 2\right)}$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + 3 = \left(Ax + B\right)\left({x}^{2} + 2\right) + \left(Cx + D\right)\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + 3 = \left(A + C\right)${x}^{3} + $\left(B + D\right)${x}^{2} + $\left(2A + C\right)$x + $\left(2B + D\right)$

On comparing coefficients both sides, we get

$\left\{$\begin{array}{ll}A + C = 0 . . . . $\left(i\right)$B + D = 1 . . . . $\left(ii\right)$2A + C = 0 . . . . $\left(iii\right)$ \\ 2B + D = 3 . . . . $\left(iv\right)$\end{array}\right

On solving, we get

$A = 0, B = 2, C = 0, D = - 1$

So,

$A + B + C + D = 1$

questions.solution: $\because x^2+x+1=\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2\begin{aligned} & \therefore \int \sqrt{x^2+x+1} d x=\int \sqrt{\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2} d x \\ & =\frac{x+\frac{1}{2}}{2} \sqrt{x^2+x+1}+\frac{3}{2} \ln \left|\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)+\sqrt{x^2+x+1}\right| \\ & =\frac{2 x+1}{4} \sqrt{x^2+x+1}+\frac{3}{8} \ln \left|\left(\frac{2 x+1}{2}\right)+\sqrt{x^2+x+1}\right| \\ & \text{$ and $} \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{x^2+x+1}} d x=\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2}} d x \\ = & \log \left|\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)+\sqrt{x^2}+x+1\right| \\ = & \log \left|\frac{2 x+1}{2}+\sqrt{x^2}+x+1\right| \\ & \text{ Now, } \int \sqrt{x^2+x+1} d x \times \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{x^2+x+1}} d x \\ = & {\left[\frac{2 x+1}{4} \sqrt{x^2+x+1}+\frac{3}{8} \log \left|\left(\frac{2 x+1}{2}\right)+\sqrt{x^2+x+1}\right|\right] } \\ & \times\left[\log \left(\frac{2 x+1}{2}+\sqrt{x^2+x+1}\right)\right]\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}=\left(\frac{2 x+1}{4} \sqrt{x^2+x+1}+\frac{3}{8} \sinh ^{-1}\right. & \left.\frac{2 x+1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) \\ & \left(\sinh ^{-1} \frac{2 x+1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)+C\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\int \mathrm{e}^x\left(\sin ^2 2 \mathrm{x}-8 \cos 4 \mathrm{x}\right) \mathrm{dx}=\mathrm{e}^x f(\mathrm{x})+\mathrm{c}$, then $f\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int e^x\left(\sin ^2 2 x-8 \cos 4 x\right) d x \\ & =\int e^x\left(\frac{1-\cos 4 x}{2}-8 \cos 4 x\right) d x \\ & =\int e^x\left(\frac{1-17 \cos 4 x}{2}\right) d x \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\int e^x d x-17 \int e^x \cos 4 x d x\right] \\ & \because \int e^{a x} \cos (b x+c) d x=\frac{e^{a x}}{a^2+b^2}[a \cos (b x+c)+b \sin (b x+c)] \\ & \therefore \quad \int e^x \cos 4 x d x=\frac{e^x}{1^2+4^2}[\cos 4 x+4 \sin 4 x] \\ & \therefore \quad \frac{1}{2}\left[e^x-17 \cdot \frac{e^x}{17}(\cos 4 x+4 \sin 4 x)\right]+C \\ & \quad=e^x\left[\frac{1}{2}-\cos 4 x-4 \sin 4 x\right]+C\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad f(x) & =\frac{1}{2}-\cos 4 x-4 \sin 4 x \\ f\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \cos \pi-\frac{4}{2} \sin \pi \\ & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}(-1)-0=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}=1 .\end{aligned}$

Let $I=\int \frac{d x}{\left(x^2-a^2\right)^{3 / 2}}$
Putting $x=a \sec \theta \Rightarrow d x=a \sec \theta \cdot \tan \theta d \theta$
$\begin{aligned}$& I=$\int \frac{a \sec \theta \cdot \tan \theta \cdot d \theta}{\left[a^2\left(\sec ^2 \theta-1\right)\right]^{\frac{3}{2}}}=\int \frac{1}{a^2} \times \frac{\sec \theta \cdot \tan \theta}{\tan ^3 \theta^2}$d $\theta$\\
&=$\frac{1}{a^2} \int \frac{1}{\cos \theta \cdot \frac{\sin ^2 \theta}{\cos ^2 \theta}}$d $\theta=\frac{1}{a^2} \int \frac{\cos \theta}{\sin ^2 \theta}$d $\theta$\\
&=$\frac{1}{a^2} \int \cot \theta \cdot \operatorname{cosec} \theta$d $\theta=-\frac{1}{a^2} \operatorname{cosec}^$2 $\theta+$C \\
&=-$\frac{x}{a^2 \sqrt{x^2-a^2}}+$C \\
&$\left(\because \sec \theta=\frac{x}{a} \Rightarrow \cos \theta=\frac{a}{x} \therefore \sin \theta=\sqrt{1-\frac{a^2}{x^2}}\right.$\\
&$\left.\quad \Rightarrow \cos \theta=\sqrt{\frac{x^2}{x^2-a^2}}=\frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2-a^2}}\right)
\end{aligned}$

Given that $\int \frac{1}{x^2+a^2} d x=\frac{1}{a} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{a}\right)+c$.
If $\int \frac{1}{x^4+3 x^2+1} d x=a \cdot \tan ^{-1} \left(\frac{b  \left(x^2-1\right)}{x}\right)
+$c \tan ^{-1}$\left(\frac{d\left(x^2+1\right)}${x}\right)+$ k where $k$ is a constant of integration, then 5(c+d+a b)=$
questions.solution:
we have $\int \frac{1}{x^4+3 x^2+1} d x$
now dividing by $\mathrm{x}^2$ to the numerator and denominator
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \int \frac{\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^2}}{\mathrm{x}^2+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^2}+3} \mathrm{dx} \\
& \Rightarrow \int \frac{\frac{1}{2}\left\{\left(1+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^2}\right)-\left(1-\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^2}\right)\right\} \mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{x}^2+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^2}+3} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} \int \frac{1+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^2}}{\left(\mathrm{x}^2+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^2}+3\right)} \mathrm{dx}-\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{1-\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^2}}{\mathrm{x}^2+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^2}+3} \mathrm{dx} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} \int \frac{1}{\left(\mathrm{x}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right)^2+5} \mathrm{dx}-\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{1}{\left(\mathrm{x}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right)^2+1} \mathrm{dx} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\left.\mathrm{x}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right)}{\sqrt{5}}\right)-\frac{1}{2} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\mathrm{x}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}}{1}\right)+\mathrm{c}
\end{aligned}$
On comparing with R.H.S
$\operatorname{atan}^{-1}\left(\frac{\mathrm{b}\left(\mathrm{x}^2-1\right)}{\mathrm{x}}\right)+\mathrm{C} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}\left(\mathrm{x}^2+1\right)}{\mathrm{x}}\right)+\mathrm{k}\Rightarrow$ we get $a=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{5}}, \mathrm{ b}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}, \mathrm{c}=\frac{-1}{2}, \mathrm{ d}=1\Rightarrow 5(\mathrm{c}+\mathrm{d}+\mathrm{ab})=3$

questions.q: $The partial fraction decomposition of \dfrac{9x - 7}{( x + 3 ) \left(x^{2} + 1\right)}$ is
questions.solution:
The partial fraction for& $\dfrac{px + q}{\left(x + a\right)\left(x^{2} + b^{2}\right)}$ is of type& $\dfrac{A}{x + a} + \dfrac{Bx + C}{x^{2} + b^{2}}$

Hence, $\dfrac{9x - 7}{\left(x + 3\right)\left(x^{2} + 1\right)} = \dfrac{A}{x + 3} + \dfrac{Bx + C}{x^{2} + 1}$

$⇒ \dfrac{9x - 7}{\left(x + 3\right)\left(x^{2} + 1\right)} = \dfrac{A \left($ x^{2} + 1\right) + $\left(Bx + C\right)\left(x + 3\right)}{ \left($ x + 3\right) $\left(x^{2} + 1\right)$}$

$⇒ 9x - 7 = A$\left(x^{2} + 1\right) + \left(Bx + C\right)\left(x + 3\right)$

$⇒ 9x - 7 = A \left(x^{2} + 1\right) + \left($ Bx^{2} + 3Bx + Cx + 3C\right)$

On comparing, the coefficients of $x^{2}, x$ and the constant term, we get

A + B = 0 . . . \left($ i\right)$

3B + C = 9 . . . \left(ii\right)$ and

A + 3C = - 7 . . . $\left($ iii\right)$

On solving the above three equations, we get A = - \dfrac{17}{5},$ B = $\dfrac{17}{5},$ C = - $\dfrac{6}{5} .

Hence, \dfrac{9x - 7}{ \left(x + 3\right) \left(x^{2} + 1\right)}$ = $\left(- \dfrac{17}{5}\right)$ x + 3 + $\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{17}{5}\right)x + \left(- \dfrac{6}{5}\right)}{x^{2} + 1}

$⇒ $\dfrac{9x - 7}{\left(x + 3\right)\left(x^{2} + 1\right)} = \dfrac{- 17}{5\left(x + 3\right)} + \left(17x - 6\right)5\left(x^{2} + 1\right) .$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f\left(x\right) + k$ is obtained by evaluating $∫ \dfrac{x3}{\left(1 + x^{2}\right)^{3}}dx,$ using the substitution $x = tan\theta$ and $g\left(x\right) + c$ is obtained by evaluating $∫ \dfrac{x3}{\left(1 + x^{2}\right)^{3}}dx,$ using the substitution $x^{2} + 1 = z,$ then $f\left(x\right) - g\left(x\right) + k - c =$
questions.solution:
${I}_{1} = ∫ \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{{\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)}^{3}}dx = f\left(x\right) + k$ 

$x = tan\theta$

$⇒ dx = {sec}^{2}\thetad\theta$

${I}_{1} = ∫ \dfrac{{tan}^{2}\theta{sec}^{2}\thetad\theta}{{\left(1 + {tan}^{2}\theta\right)}^{3}}$

${I}_{1} = ∫ \dfrac{{tan}^{3}\theta{sec}^{2}\thetad\theta}{{sec}^{6}\theta}$

${I}_{1} = ∫ {sin}^{3}\thetacos\thetad\theta$

Let $sin\theta = p$

$⇒ cos\thetad\theta = dp$

${I}_{1} = {∫}_{}^{}{p}^{3}dp = \dfrac{{p}^{4}}{4} + k$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = \dfrac{{sin}^{4}\theta}{4} + k$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = \dfrac{{sin}^{4}\left[{tan}^{- 1}x\right]}{4} + k$

Let ${tan}^{- 1}x = \alpha ⇒ x = tan\alpha$

$⇒ sin\alpha = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{2}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{sin}^{4}\alpha}{4} = \dfrac{{x}^{4}}{4\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)} + k = f\left(x\right) + k$

Now $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{{x}^{4}}{4\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)}$

${I}_{1} = {∫}_{}^{}\dfrac{{x}^{3}}{{\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)}^{3}}dx = g\left(x\right) + c$

Let $1 + {x}^{2} = z ⇒ {x}^{2} = z - 1$

$⇒ xdx = \dfrac{1}{2}dz$

${I}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{z - 1}{{z}^{3}}dz$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(\dfrac{1}{{z}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{z}^{3}}\right)dz$

${I}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{- 1}{z} + \dfrac{1}{2{z}^{2}}\right]$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{- 1}{1 + {x}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{2{\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)}^{2}}\right]$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = \left[\dfrac{- 2{x}^{2} - 1}{4{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)}^{2}}\right] + c = \left[g ( x ) + c\right]$

$⇒ g ( x ) = \left[\dfrac{- 2{x}^{2} - 1}{4{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)}^{2}}\right]$

Now $f\left(x\right) - g\left(x\right) + k - c =$$\dfrac{{x}^{4}}{4\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)} - \left[\dfrac{- 2{x}^{2} - 1}{4{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)}^{2}}\right]$

$= \dfrac{{x}^{4} + 2{x}^{2} + 1}{4{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)}^{2}} + k - c$

$= \dfrac{1}{4} + k - c$

Hence, it is a constant.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
For $- 1 < x < 1$ and $y > 1,$~if $∫ \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 + x} + \sqrt{1 - x}}dx + ∫ \dfrac{y}{\sqrt{y + 1} + \sqrt{y - 1}}dy =$
$A\left(1 + x\right)3 / 2 + B\left(1 - x\right)3 / 2 + f\left(y\right)\left(y + 1\right)3 / 2 + g\left(y\right)\left(y - 1\right)3 / 2 + C,$~then $Af\left(y\right) + Bg\left(y\right) =$
questions.solution:
Given, $∫ \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 + x} + \sqrt{1 - x}}dx + ∫ \dfrac{y}{\sqrt{y + 1} + \sqrt{y - 1}}dy = A{\left(1 + x\right)}^{3 / 2} + B{\left(1 - x\right)}^{3 / 2} + f\left(y\right){\left(y + 1\right)}^{3 / 2} + g\left(y\right){\left(y - 1\right)}^{3 / 2} + C . . . . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

Let, ${I}_{1} = ∫ \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 + x} + \sqrt{1 - x}}dx$

Multiplying and dividing by $\left(\sqrt{1 + x} - \sqrt{1 - x}\right)$

${I}_{1} = ∫ \dfrac{x\left(\sqrt{1 + x} - \sqrt{1 - x}\right)}{\left(\sqrt{1 + x} + \sqrt{1 - x}\right)\left(\sqrt{1 + x} - \sqrt{1 - x}\right)}dx$

${I}_{1} = ∫ \dfrac{x\left(\sqrt{1 + x} - \sqrt{1 - x}\right)}{2x}dx$

${I}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \sqrt{1 + x}dx - \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \sqrt{1 - x}dx$

${I}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(x + 1\right)\dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{1}{3}\left(1 - x\right)\dfrac{3}{2} + C . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . \left(ii\right)$

Let ${I}_{2} = ∫ \dfrac{y}{\sqrt{y + 1} + \sqrt{y - 1}}dy$

Multiplying and dividing by $\left(\sqrt{y + 1} - \sqrt{y - 1}\right)$

${I}_{2} = ∫ \dfrac{y\left(\sqrt{y + 1} - \sqrt{y - 1}\right)}{\left(\sqrt{y + 1} + \sqrt{y - 1}\right)\sqrt{y + 1} - \sqrt{y - 1}}dy$

$∴ {I}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ y\sqrt{y + 1}dx - \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ y\sqrt{y - 1}dx$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(\left(y + 1\right) - 1\right)\left(y + 1\right)\dfrac{1}{2}dy - \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(\left(y - 1\right) + 1\right)\left(y - 1\right)\dfrac{1}{2}dy$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(\left(y + 1\right)\dfrac{3}{2} - \left(y + 1\right)\dfrac{1}{2}\right)dy - \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(\left(y - 1\right)\dfrac{3}{2} + \left(y - 1\right)\dfrac{1}{2}\right)dy$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{5}\left(y + 1\right)\dfrac{5}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3}\left(y + 1\right)\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{5}\left(y - 1\right)\dfrac{5}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3}\left(y - 1\right)\dfrac{3}{2} + {C}_{1} . . . . . . . . . . . . \left(iii\right)$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = \dfrac{\left(3y - 2\right)}{15}\left(y + 1\right)\dfrac{3}{2} - \left(y - 1\right)\dfrac{3}{2}\dfrac{\left(3y + 2\right)}{15} + {C}_{1} . . . . . . . . . . . . \left(iii\right)$

questions.q: If $∫ \dfrac{x + 3}{\left(x - 1\right)^{2}\left(2x - 1\right)}dx = \dfrac{A}{x - 1} + Blog\left(2x - 1\right) + Clog\left(x - 1\right) + K$ then $A + B + C =$
questions.solution:
Given,

$∫ \dfrac{x + 3}{{\left(x - 1\right)}^{2}\left(2x - 1\right)}dx = \dfrac{A}{x - 1} + Blog\left(2x - 1\right) + Clog\left(x - 1\right) + K$

Now solving $\dfrac{x + 3}{{\left(x - 1\right)}^{2}\left(2x - 1\right)}$ by partial fraction we get,

$\dfrac{x + 3}{{\left(x - 1\right)}^{2}\left(2x - 1\right)} = \dfrac{\alpha}{x - 1} + \dfrac{\beta}{{\left(x - 1\right)}^{2}} + \dfrac{\gamma}{\left(2x - 1\right)}$

$⇒ x + 3 = \alpha\left(x - 1\right)\left(2x - 1\right) + \beta\left(2x - 1\right) + \gamma{\left(x - 1\right)}^{2}$

Now comparing coefficient of ${x}^{2}, x \text{ and } \text{constant term}$ we get,

$\alpha = - 7, \beta = 4 \text{ and } \gamma = 14$

Now putting the value and integrating the given function we get,

$∫ \dfrac{x + 3}{{\left(x - 1\right)}^{2}\left(2x - 1\right)} = ∫ \dfrac{- 7}{x - 1} + ∫ \dfrac{4}{{\left(x - 1\right)}^{2}} + ∫ \dfrac{14}{\left(2x - 1\right)}$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{x + 3}{{\left(x - 1\right)}^{2}\left(2x - 1\right)} = - 7log\left(x - 1\right) + \dfrac{- 4}{\left(x - 1\right)} + 7log\left(2x - 1\right) + K$

Now comparing with $∫ \dfrac{x + 3}{{\left(x - 1\right)}^{2}\left(2x - 1\right)}dx = \dfrac{A}{x - 1} + Blog\left(2x - 1\right) + Clog\left(x - 1\right) + K$

We get,

$A = - 7, B - 4 \text{ and } C = 7$

Then $A + B + C = - 4$

We have,

Let
$\begin{aligned}
I & =\int \frac{(x-1) d x}{(x+1) \sqrt{x^3+x^2+x}} \\
& =\int \frac{x-1}{x(x+1) \sqrt{x+\frac{1}{x}+1}} d x

Put,
$\begin{aligned}
x+\frac{1}{x}+1 & =t \text{$ and $}\left(1-\frac{1}{x^2}\right) d x=d t \\

= & 2 \tan ^{-1} \sqrt{t}+C=2 \tan ^{-1} \sqrt{x+\frac{1}{x}+1}+C
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad A=2 \Rightarrow f(x)=x+\frac{1}{x}+1 \\ & A=2 \Rightarrow f(-1)=-1-1+1=-1 \\ & \therefore \quad(A, f(-1)=(2,-1) \\ & \end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $f\left(\frac{2 x+3}{3 x+5}\right)=x+4, x \neq \frac{-5}{3}, \frac{2}{3}$ and $\int f(x) d x=A x+B \ln |3 x-2|+C$, then $3 B-A=$
questions.solution:
We have, $f\left(\frac{2 x+3}{3 x+5}\right)=x+4\begin{aligned}
& \text{ Put, } \frac{2 x+3}{3 x+5}=y \Rightarrow 2 x+3=3 x y+5 y \Rightarrow x=\frac{5 y-3}{2-3 y} \\
& \therefore f(y)=\frac{5 y-3}{2-3 y}+4=\frac{5 y-3+8-12 y}{2-3 y} \Rightarrow f(y)=\frac{7 y-5}{3 x-2} \\
& \therefore \quad f(x)=\frac{7 x-5}{3 x-2} \Rightarrow \int f(x) d x=\int \frac{7 x-5}{3 x-2} d x
\end{aligned}$
Put, $3 x-2=t \Rightarrow x=\frac{t+2}{3}\begin{aligned}
d x & =\frac{d t}{3}=\frac{1}{3} \int \frac{7\left(\frac{t+2}{3}\right)-5}{t} d t \\
& =\frac{1}{9} \int \frac{7 t-1}{t} d t=\frac{7}{9} \int d t-\frac{1}{3} \int \frac{d t}{t} \\
& =\frac{7}{9} t-\frac{1}{9} \log t+C \\
& =\frac{7}{9}(3 x-2)-\frac{1}{9} \log |3 x-2|+C \\
& =\frac{7}{3} x-\frac{1}{9} \log |^{3} x-2|+C
\end{aligned}$
Here, A=$\frac{7}{3}$, B=-$\frac{1}{9}$\therefore \quad 3 B-A=3 $\left(-\frac{1}{9}\right)-\frac{7}{3}=$-$\frac{8}{3}$

questions.q: $\begin{aligned} & \text{ If } 5(f(x))^2=x f(x)+30 \text{$ and $} \\ & \int \frac{\left(3 x^3+\left(1-30 x^2\right) f(x)\right)}{(10 f(x)-x)\left(x^3-f(x)\right)^2} d x \\ & =\frac{A}{B x^3+D f(x)}+C \text{ then } A+B+D=\end{aligned}$
questions.solution:
We have,
$\begin{aligned}
& 5(f(x))^2=x f(x)+30 \Rightarrow 10 f(x) f^{\prime}(x)=x f^{\prime}(x)+f(x) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad(10 f(x)-x) f^{\prime}(x)=f(x)
\end{aligned}$
Now, $I=\int \frac{\left(3 x^3+\left(1-30 x^2\right) f(x)\right)}{(10 f(x)-x)\left(x^3-f(x)\right)^2} d x\begin{aligned}
& =\int \frac{3 x^3-30 x^2 f(x)+f(x)}{(10 f(x)-x)\left(x^3-f(x)\right)^2} d x \\
& =\int \frac{3 x^2(x-10 f(x))+(10 f(x)-x) f^{\prime}(x)}{(10 f(x)-x)\left(x^3-f(x)\right)^2} d x \\
& =\int \frac{-(10 f(x)-x)\left(3 x^2-f(x)\right)}{(10 f(x)-x)\left(x^3-f(x)\right)^3} d x \\
& =-\int \frac{3 x^2-f(x)}{\left(x^3-f(x)\right)^2} d x
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \text{ put } x^3-f(x)=t \\
& \Rightarrow \quad\left(3 x^2-f^{\prime}(x)\right) f(x)=d t \\
& \therefore \quad I=-\int \frac{d t}{t^2}=\frac{1}{t}+c \Rightarrow I=\frac{1}{x^3-f(x)}+c \\
& \therefore \quad A=1, B=1, D=-1, \\
& \therefore A+B+D=1+1-1=1
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $\begin{aligned} & \text{ If } \int x[\log (1+x)]^3 d x=\frac{(1+x)^2}{16}(f(x)) \\ & +(1+x)(g(x)), \text{ then } f(x)+g(x)=\end{aligned}$
questions.solution:
We have,
$\begin{aligned} & \int x[\log (1+x)]^3 d x=\frac{(1+x)^2}{16} f(x)+(1+x) g(x) \\ & \text{ Let } I=\int x[\log (1+x)]^3 d x \\ & \text{ put } \log (1+x)=t \Rightarrow 1+x=e^t \Rightarrow d x=e^t d t \\ & \therefore \quad I=\int\left(e^t-1\right) t^3 e^t d t \Rightarrow I=\int\left(e^{2 t} t^3-e^t t^3\right) d t \\ & I=e^{2 t}\left(\frac{t^3}{2}-\frac{3 t^2}{4}+\frac{6 t}{8}-\frac{6}{16}\right) \\ & -e^t\left(t^3-3 t^2+6 t-6\right)+c \\ & I=(1+x)^2 \\ & {\left[\frac{(\log (1+x))^3}{2}-3 \frac{(\log (1+x))^2}{4}+\frac{6 \log (1+x)}{8}-\frac{6}{16}\right]} \\ & -(1+x)\left[(\log (1+x))^3-3(\log (1+x))^2\right. \\ & +6(\log (1+x)-6] \\ & \because \quad f(x)=8(\log (1+x))^3-12(\log (1+x))^2 \\ & +12 \log (1+x)-6 \\ & \text{ and, } \quad g(x)=-(\log (1+x))^3+3(\log (1+x))^2 \\ & -6 \log (1+x)+6 \\ & f(x)+g(x)=7(\log (1+x))^3-9(\log (1+x))^2 \\ & +6 \log (1+x)+C \\ & \end{aligned}$

questions.solution:

$\int \frac{x^2}{\left(\sqrt{4-x^2}\right)^3} d x$...(i)
Substituting, $x=2 \sin \theta$ and $d x=2 \cos \theta d \theta$ Putting in Eq. (i),
$=\int \frac{(2 \sin \theta)^2}{\left.(\sqrt{4-(2 \sin \theta})^2\right)^3} 2 \cos \theta d \theta=\int \frac{4 \times 2 \times \sin ^2 \theta \cos \theta d \theta}{\left(\sqrt{4-4 \sin ^2 \theta}\right)^3}=\int \frac{8 \sin ^2 \theta \cos \theta d \theta}{(2 \cos \theta)^3}=\int \frac{\sin ^2 \theta \cos \theta}{\cos ^3 \theta} d \theta=\int \tan ^2 \theta d \theta=\int\left(\sec ^2 \theta-1\right) d \theta=\int \sec ^2 \theta d \theta-\int d \theta=\tan \theta-\theta+C$

questions.q: If $∫ \dfrac{1}{( x - 2{)}^{5} ( x - 1{)}^{4}}dx = \mathop{∑}_{r = - 4}^{- 1}{A}_{r}\left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 1}\right)r + \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{3}{A}_{r}\left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 1}\right)r + Bf\left(x\right),$ then $f\left(x\right) =$
questions.solution:
$I = ∫ \dfrac{1}{{\left(x - 2\right)}^{5} . {\left(x - 1\right)}^{4}}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{{\left(x - 2\right)}^{9} . {\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x - 2}\right)}^{4}}$

Let $\dfrac{x - 1}{x - 2} = t$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(x - 2\right) . 1 - \left(x - 1\right) . 1}{{\left(x - 2\right)}^{2}}dx = dt$

$⇒ \dfrac{- 1}{{\left(x - 2\right)}^{2}}dx = dt . . . \left(1\right)$

Also, $\dfrac{x - 1}{x - 2} = t$

$⇒ x - 1 = tx - 2t$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{2t - 1}{t - 1}$

$⇒ x - 2 = \dfrac{1}{t - 1} . . . \left(2\right)$

$∴ I = ∫ \dfrac{- dt}{\dfrac{1}{{\left(t - 1\right)}^{7}}}{t}^{4}$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{{\left(1 - t\right)}^{7}}{{t}^{4}}dt$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{1 - c1 7 t + c2 7 {t}^{2} - c3 7 {t}^{3} + . . . . . . + c6 7 . {t}^{6} - c7 7 {t}^{7}}{{t}^{4}}dt$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{1}{{t}^{4}}dt - c1 7 ∫ \dfrac{dt}{{t}^{3}} + c2 7 ∫ \dfrac{dt}{{t}^{2}} - c3 7 ∫ \dfrac{1}{t}dt + . . . . - c7 7 ∫ {t}^{3}dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{{t}^{- 4 + 1}}{- 4 + 1} - 7\dfrac{{t}^{- 3 + 1}}{- 3 + 1} + c2 7 \dfrac{{t}^{- 2 + 1}}{- 2 + 1} - c3 7 log\left|t\right| + . . . - \dfrac{{t}^{4}}{4} + c$

  $⇒ I = \dfrac{- 1}{3}{\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x - 2}\right)}^{- 3} + \dfrac{7}{2}{\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x - 2}\right)}^{- 2} - c3 7 log\left|\dfrac{x - 1}{x - 2}\right| + . . . . . - \dfrac{1}{4}{\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x - 2}\right)}^{4} + c$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{- 1}{3}{\left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 1}\right)}^{3} + \dfrac{7}{2}{\left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 1}\right)}^{2} + c2 7 \left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 1}\right) + c4 7 {\left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 1}\right)}^{- 1} + c3 7 \left[log\left(x - 2\right) - log\left(x - 1\right)\right] . . . . - \dfrac{1}{4}{\left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 1}\right)}^{- 4} + c . . . \left(1\right)$

$∵$Given that

$∫ \dfrac{1}{( x - 2{)}^{5} ( x - 1{)}^{4}}dx = \mathop{∑}_{r = - 4}^{- 1}{A}_{r}{\left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 1}\right)}^{r} + \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{3}{A}_{r}{\left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 1}\right)}^{r} + Bf\left(x\right)$

$∴$We get $f\left(x\right) = log\left(x - 2\right) - log\left(x - 1\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \frac{d x}{x \ln (x) \ln ^2(x) \ln ^3(x) \ldots \ln ^m(x)}=\frac{(\ln (x))^K}{K}+C\Rightarrow 2 K=$
questions.solution:
Given that,
$\int \frac{d x}{x \ln (x) \ln ^2(x) \ln ^3(x) \ldots \ln ^m(x)}$ ...(i)
Substituting, $\ln x=u$ Differentiating w.r.t ' $x$ ', $\frac{1}{x} d x=d u$
Putting in Eq. (i)
$\int \frac{d u}{u u^2 u^3 \ldots u^m} \text{ or } \int \frac{d u}{u^{1+2+3+\ldots+m}}
or \quad \int \frac{d u}{u^{\frac{m(m+1)}{2}}} \quad\left\{1+2+3++n=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right\}
or \quad \int u^{\frac{-m(m+1)}{2}} d u=\frac{u^{\frac{-m(m+1)}{2}+1}}{\frac{-m(m+1)}{2}+1}+C\left[\because \int x^n d x=\frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}\right]=\frac{\frac{u(m+2)(1-m)}{2}}{\frac{(m+2)(1-m)}{2}}+C$
Now, putting the value of $u$.
$=\frac{(\ln (x)) \frac{(m+2)(1-m)}{2}}{\frac{(m-2)(1-m)}{2}}+C$
Comparing with given form,
$K=\frac{(m+2)(1-m)}{2} \text{ and } 2 K=(m+2)(1-m)$

questions.q: If $I_m=\int x^m \cos n x d x=g(x)-\frac{m(m-1)}{n^2} I_{m-2}$, then $g(x)=$
questions.solution:
Given that,
$I_m=\int x^m \cos n x d x=g(x)-\frac{m(m-1)}{n^2} I_{m-2}\ldots(i)I_{m-2}=\int x^{m-2} \cos n x d x$
Solving integration by parts
$\left.=\cos n x \int x^{m-2} d x-\int\left(\frac{d}{d x} \cos n x\right) \int x^{m-2} d x\right) d x=\cos n x\left[\frac{x^{m-1}}{m-1}\right]+n \int \sin n x \frac{x^{m-1}}{m-1} d xI_{m-2}=\frac{x^{m-1} \cos n x}{m-1}+\frac{n}{m-1} \int x^{m-1} \sin n x d x$
Again integrating by parts method,
$I_{m-2}=\frac{x^{m-1} \cos n x}{m-1}+\frac{n}{m-1}\left\{\sin n x \int x^{m-1} d x-\int\left(\frac{d}{d x} \sin n x \int x^{m-1} d x\right) d x\right\}=\frac{x^{m-1} \cos n x}{m-1}+\frac{n}{m-1}\left\{\frac{\sin n x \cdot x^m}{m}-\int n \cdot \cos n x \frac{x^m}{m} d x\right\}=\frac{x^{m-1} \cos n x}{m-1}+\frac{n}{m-1} \cdot \frac{1}{m}\left\{x^m \sin n x-n \int x^m \cos n x d x\right\}=\frac{x^{m-1} \cos n x}{m-1}+\frac{n}{m(m-1)}\left(x^m \sin n x-n I_m\right)I_{m-2}=\frac{x^{m-1} \cos n x}{m-1}+\frac{n}{m(m-1)} x^m \sin n x-\frac{n^2}{m(m-1)} I_m$ or $\frac{n^2}{m(m-1)} I_m=\frac{x^{m-1} \cos n x}{m-1}+\frac{n}{m(m-1)} x^m\sin n x-I_{m-2}
or I_m=\frac{m(m-1)}{n^2}\left[\frac{x^{m-1} \cos n x}{m-1}+\frac{n}{m(m-1)} x^m \sin n x-I_{m-2}\right]I_m=\frac{m}{n^2} x^{m-1} \cos n x+\frac{x^m \sin n x}{n}-\frac{m(m-1)}{n^2} I_{m-2}$
On comparing with Eq. (i), we get
$g(x)=\frac{x^m \sin n x}{n}+\frac{m}{n^2} x^{m-1} \cos n x$

questions.q: Let $I_n=\int \sec ^n x d x$. If $5 I_6-4 I_4=f(x)$, then $f  \left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)is equal to$
questions.solution:
Given that,
$I_n=\int \sec ^n x d xf(x)=5 I_6-4 I_4=5 \int \sec ^6 x d x-4 \int \sec ^4 x d x=\int 5 \sec ^4 x \sec ^2 x d x-\int 4 \sec ^2 x \sec ^2 x d xf(x)=\int\left\{5\left(1+\tan ^2 x\right)^2-4\left(1+\tan ^2 x\right)\right\} \sec ^2 x d x$
Let $u=\tan x$
Differentiating w.r.t. ' $x$ ', we get
$d u=\sec ^2 x d x\therefore \quad f(x)=\int\left\{5\left(1+u^2\right)^2-4\left(1+u^2\right)\right\} d u=\int\left\{5\left(1+u^4+2 u^2\right)-4\left(1+u^2\right)\right\} d u=\int\left(5+5 u^4+10 u^2-4-4 u^2\right) d u=\int\left(5 u^4+6 u^2+1\right) d u=5 \frac{u^5}{5}+6 \frac{u^3}{3}+uf(x)=u^5+2 u^3+uf(x)=(\tan x)^5+2(\tan x)^3+\tan x$
At $x=\frac{\pi}{4}, f\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\left(\tan \frac{\pi}{4}\right)^5+2\left(\tan \frac{\pi}{4}\right)^3+\tan \frac{\pi}{4}=(1)^5+2(1)^3+(1)f\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=4$

questions.q: If $\int e^{\sin ^2 x}\left(\sin x \cos x+\cos ^3 x \sin x\right) d x=e^{\sin ^2 x}(1+f(x))+c$, then $f^{\prime}(x)=$
questions.solution:
$I=\int e^{\sin ^2 x}\left(\sin x \cos x+\cos ^3 x \sin x\right) d x=\int e^{\sin ^2 x}\left(1+\cos ^2 x\right) \sin x \cos x d x=\int e^{\sin ^2 x}\left(2-\sin ^2 x\right) \sin x \cos x d x$
Let $\sin ^2 x=t \Rightarrow \sin x \cos x d x=\frac{d t}{2}\therefore I=\frac{1}{2} \int e^t(2-t) d t=e^t-\frac{1}{2}\left[t \cdot e^t-e^t\right]+C=e^t\left[1-\frac{t}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\right]+C=e^{\sin ^2 x}\left[1+\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sin ^2 x}{2}\right]+C=e^{\sin ^2 x}[1+f(x)]+C$(given)
Therefore, $f(x)=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sin ^2 x}{2} \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x)=-\frac{1}{2} \sin 2 x$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int x^3(\log x)^2 d x=x^4\left[A(\log x)^2+B(\log x)\right.+C \log e]+K$, then $A+B+C$
questions.solution:
We have,
$\int x^3(\log x)^2 d x=x^4\left[A(\log x)^2+B(\log x)+C \log e\right]+K$
Now, $\int x^3(\log x)^2 d x=(\log x)^2 \int x^3 d x-\int\left(\frac{d}{d x}(\log x)^2 \int x^3 d x\right) d x\left.=(\log x)^2 \cdot \frac{x^4}{4}-\int(2 \log x) \cdot \frac{1}{x} \cdot \frac{x^4}{4}\right) d x=(\log x)^2\left(\frac{x^4}{4}\right)-\frac{1}{2} \int \log x \cdot x^3 d x=(\log x)^2\left(\frac{x^4}{4}\right)-\frac{1}{2}\left[\log x \int x^3 d x-\int\left(\frac{d}{d x}\left(\log x \int x^3 d x\right) d x\right]\right.=(\log x)^2\left(\frac{x^4}{4}\right)-\frac{1}{2}\left[\log x\left(\frac{x^4}{4}\right)-\int \frac{1}{x} \cdot \frac{x^4}{4} d x\right]=(\log x)^2\left(\frac{x^4}{4}\right)-\frac{1}{2}\left[\log x\left(\frac{x^4}{4}\right)-\frac{1}{4} \cdot \int x^3 d x\right]=(\log x)^2\left(\frac{x^4}{4}\right)-\frac{1}{2}\left[\log x\left(\frac{x^4}{4}\right)-\frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{x^4}{4}\right]+K=x^4\left[\frac{1}{4}(\log x)^2-\frac{1}{8} \log x+\frac{1}{32} \log e\right]+K\therefore A=\frac{1}{4}, B=\frac{-1}{8}$ and $C=\frac{1}{32}\therefore A+B+C=\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{32}=\frac{8-4+1}{32}=\frac{5}{32}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int \frac{x^2\left(x \sec ^2 x+\tan x\right)}{(x \tan x+1)^2} d x=A \log(|x \sin x+\cos x|)+B \frac{f(x)}{(x \tan x+1)}+C$, then $f(A+B)=$
questions.solution:
Let $I=\int x^2 \cdot \frac{x \sec ^2 x+\tan x}{(x \tan x+1)^2} d x=x^2\left(-\frac{1}{(x \tan x+1)}\right)-\int 2 x\left(-\frac{1}{(x \tan x+1}\right) d x\left[\right.$ since $\left.\int \frac{x \sec ^2 x+\tan x}{(x \tan x+1)^2}=\int \frac{d t}{t^2}=-\frac{1}{t}=-\frac{1}{(x \tan x+1)}\right]=-\left(\frac{x^2}{x \tan x+1}\right)+\int \frac{2 x \cos x}{(x \sin x+\cos x)} d x$
[putting $x \sin x+\cos x=u\Rightarrow(x \cos x+\sin x-\sin x) d x=d u]=\frac{-x^2}{(x \tan x+1)}+2 \int \frac{d u}{u}=\frac{-x^2}{x \tan x+1}+2 \log |u|+C=\frac{-x^2}{x \tan x+1}+2 \log |x \sin x+\cos x|+C\therefore A=2$ and $B=-1 and f(x)=x^2\therefore f(A+B)=f(2-1)=f(1)=(1)^2=1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int \frac{9 x+15}{x^3-6 x-9} d x=A \log |g(x)|+B \log |f(x)|+C$, then $\frac{(A-B) g(4)}{f(-1)}=$
questions.solution:
We have,
$\int \frac{9 x+15}{x^3-6 x-9} d x=A \log |g(x)|+B \log |f(x)|+C$
Now, $\frac{9 x+15}{x^3-6 x-9}=\frac{9 x+15}{(x-3)\left(x^2+3 x+3\right)}\therefore \frac{9 x+15}{(x-3)\left(x^2+3 x+3\right)}=\frac{A}{x-3}+\frac{B x+C}{x^2+3 x+3}\Rightarrow 9 x+15=A\left(x^2+3 x+3\right)+(B x+c)(x-3)\Rightarrow 9 x+15=x^2(A+B)+x(3 A-3 B+C)+(3 A-3 C)$
On equating coefficients of $x^2, x$ and constant term, we get
A+B=0,3 A-3 B+C=9 $\text{$ and } 3 A-3 C=15$
On solving above three equations we get, A=2, B=-2$ and $C=-3\therefore \int \frac{9 x+15}{(x-3)\left(x^2+3 x+3\right)} d x=\int \frac{2}{x-3} d x+\int \frac{-2 x-3}{x^2+3 x+3} d x=\int \frac{2}{x-3} d x-\int \frac{2 x+3}{x^2+3 x+3} d x=2 \log |x-3|-\log \left|x^2+3 x+3\right|+C\therefore A=2, B=-1, g(x)=x-3$ and $f(x)=x^2+3 x+3\therefore \quad \frac{(A-B) g(4)}{f(-1)}=\frac{(2+1)(4-3)}{(-1)^2+3(-1)+3}=3$

questions.q: $\begin{aligned} & \text{ If } \frac{4 x^2+5 x^4+7}{\left(x^2+1\right)\left(x^4+x^2+1\right)}=\frac{A x+B}{x^2+1} \\ & +\frac{C x^3+D x^2+E x+F}{x^4+x^2+1}, \text{ then } \\ & B+2(D+F+E)-C \cdot A=\end{aligned}$
questions.solution:
We have,
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{4 x^2+5 x^4+7}{\left(x^2+1\right)\left(x^4+x^2+1\right)}=\frac{A x+B}{x^2+1}+\frac{C x^3+D x^2+E x+F}{x^4+x^2+1} \\
& \Rightarrow 4 x^2+5 x^4+7=(A x+B)\left(x^4+x^2+1\right) \\
& +\left(C x^3+D x^2+E x+F\right)\left(x^2+1\right) \\
& \Rightarrow 5 x^4+4 x^2+7=A x^5+A x^3+A x+B x^4+B x^2 \\
& +B+C x^5+C x^3+D x^4+D x^2+E x^3+E x+F x^2+F \\
& \Rightarrow 5 x^4+4 x^2+7=(A+C) x^5+(B+D) x^4 \\
& +(A+C+E) x^3+(B+D+F) x^2+(A+E) x+(B+F) \\
\end{aligned}$
On comparing, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& A+C=0 \\
& B+D=5
\end{aligned}\begin{array}{r}
A+C+E=0 \\
B+D+F=4 \\
A+E=0 \\
B+F=7
\end{array}
On solving, we get \begin{gathered}$ A=C=E=0, B=8 . D=-3, F=-1 \\
\therefore B+2(D+F+E)-C $\cdot$ A=8+2(-3-1+0)-0 $\times0 \\
=8-8=0
\end{gathered}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: For $k \in(1, \infty), \int \frac{1}{1+k \cos x} d x=$
questions.solution:
Let $\begin{aligned} I & =\int \frac{1}{1+k \cos x} d x=\int \frac{1}{1+k\left(\frac{1-\tan ^2 x / 2}{1+\tan ^2 x / 2}\right)} d x \\ & =\int \frac{\sec ^2 x / 2}{1+\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}+k-k \tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}} d x \\ & =\int \frac{\sec ^2 \frac{x}{2}}{(k+1)-(k-1) \tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}} d x\end{aligned}$
Put, $\tan \frac{x}{2}=t \Rightarrow \sec ^2 \frac{x}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2} d x=d t \Rightarrow \sec ^2 \frac{x}{2} d x=2 d t\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad I & =2 \int \frac{d t}{(k+1)-(k-1) t^2}=\frac{2}{k-1} \int \frac{d t}{\left(\sqrt{\frac{k+1}{k-1}}\right)^2-t^2} \\
& =\frac{2}{k-1} \cdot \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{\frac{k+1}{k-1}}} \log \left[\frac{\sqrt{\frac{k+1}{k-1}}+t}{\sqrt{\frac{k+1}{k-1}}-t}\right]+C \\
& =\frac{1}{\sqrt{k^2-1}} \log \left[\frac{\sqrt{k+1}+\sqrt{k-1} \tan \frac{x}{2}}{\sqrt{k+1}-\sqrt{k-1} \tan \frac{x}{2}}\right]+C
\end{aligned}$

Let $I = ∫ ( x + 2 ) \sqrt{x + 3}dx$

Let $\sqrt{x + 3} =$t$

Differentiating both sides,

\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x + 3}}dx = dt$

$⇒ dx = 2\sqrt{x + 3}dt$

Using in the function to be integrated,

$I = ∫ ( x + 2 ) \left(\sqrt{x + 3}\right)\left(2\sqrt{x + 3}\right)dt$

$= 2 ∫ ( x + 2 ) ( x + 3 ) dt$

$= 2 ∫ \left(t^{2} - 1\right)\left(t^{2}\right)dt$

$= 2 ∫ \left(t^{4} - t^{2}\right)dt$

$= 2\left(\dfrac{t5}{5} - \dfrac{t3}{3}\right) + C$

$= \dfrac{2}{15}\left(t\right)\left(t^{2}\right)\left(3t^{2} - 5\right) + C$

$= \dfrac{2}{15}\sqrt{x + 3}\left(x + 3\right)\left(3\left(x + 3\right) - 5\right) + C= \dfrac{2}{15}\sqrt{x + 3}\left(x + 3\right)\left(3x - 4\right) + C$

questions.q: If $\int \frac{(x-1) d x}{(x+1) \sqrt{x^3+x^2+x}}=f(x)+C$, then $f(1)=$
questions.solution:
Let $I=\int \frac{x-1}{(x+1) \sqrt{x^3+x^2+x}} d x\begin{aligned} & =\int \frac{(x-1)(x+1)}{(x+1)(x+1) \sqrt{x^3+x^2+x}} d x \\ & =\int \frac{x^2-1}{(x+1)^2 \sqrt{x^3+x^2+x}} d x \\ & =\int \frac{x^2-1}{\left(x^2+2 x+1\right) \sqrt{x^3+x^2+x}} d x \\ & =\int \frac{x^2\left(1-1 / x^2\right) d x}{x\left(x+2+\frac{1}{x}\right) \cdot x \sqrt{x+1+\frac{1}{x}}} \\ & =\int \frac{1-\frac{1}{x^2}}{\left(x+\frac{1}{x}+2\right) \sqrt{x+\frac{1}{x}+1}}\end{aligned}$
Put, $x+\frac{1}{x}+1=t^2 \Rightarrow\left(1-\frac{1}{x^2}\right) d x=2 t d t\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad I & =\int \frac{2 t d t}{\left(t^2+1\right) t}=2 \int \frac{d t}{t^2+1}=2 \tan ^{-1} t \\ & =2 \tan ^{-1}\left(\sqrt{x+\frac{1}{x}+1}\right)+C\end{aligned}\therefore \quad f(x)=2 \tan ^{-1}\left(\sqrt{x+\frac{1}{x}+1}\right)\therefore \quad f(1)=2 \tan ^{-1} \sqrt{3}=2 \times \frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{2 \pi}{3}$

We have,
$\begin{array}{r}\frac{x^4+3 x+1}{(x+1)^2(x-1)}=A$ x+B+$\frac{C}{x+1}+\frac{D}{(x+1)^2}+\frac{E}{x-1} \\ \Rightarrow x^4+3 x+1=A x(x+1)^2(x-1)+B(x+1)^2(x-1) \\ \quad+C(x+1)(x-1)+D(x-1)+E(x+1)^2 \\ \Rightarrow x^4+3 x+1=A x\left(x^3+x^2-x-1\right) \\ +B\left(x^3-1 x^2-x-1\right)+C\left(x^2-1\right)$ \\ \quad+D(x-1)+E$\left(x^2+2 x+1\right)$ \\ \Rightarrow x^4+3 x+1=A x^4+(A+B) x^3 \\ +(-A+B+C+E) x^2+(-A-B+D+2 E) x \\ +(-B-C-D+E)\end{array} $\begin{aligned}A & =1 \\ A+B & =0 \\ -A+B+C+E & =0 \\ -A-B+D+2 E & =3 \\ -B-C-D+E & =1\end{aligned}\therefore \quad A=1, B=-1, C= \frac{+3}{4} ,$ D=$\frac{1}{2},$ E= $\frac{5}{4}$\begin{gathered}\therefore \quadA+$B+C+D+E=1-1+\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{2}$+$\frac{5}{4}$\\ =$\frac{+3+2+5}{4}=\frac{10}{4}=\frac{5}{2} .\end{gathered}$

But it is given, $\lambda=\frac{7}{41}$ and $\mu=\frac{22}{41}a=3, b=4\int \frac{d x}{b+a \cos x}=\int \frac{d x}{4+3 \cos x}=\int \frac{\left(1+\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}\right) d x}{4\left(1+\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}\right)+3\left(1-\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}\right)}\begin{aligned} &=\int \frac{\sec ^2 x / 2}{7+\tan ^2 x / 2} d x \\ & \tan \frac{x}{2}=t \Rightarrow \sec ^2 \frac{x}{2} d x=2 d t \\ & \frac{d x}{b+a \cos x}=2 \int \frac{d t}{7+t^2} \\ &=\frac{2}{\sqrt{7}} \tan ^{-1} \frac{t}{\sqrt{7}}+C \\ &=\frac{2}{\sqrt{7}} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\tan x / 2}{\sqrt{7}}\right)+C\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $\int \frac{3 \sin x+5 \cos x+4}{\sin x+\cos x+2} d x=$
questions.solution:
$I=\int \frac{3 \sin x+5 \cos x+4}{\sin x+\cos x+2} d x$
Let $(3 \sin x+5 \cos x+4)=A(\sin x+\cos x+2)+B \frac{d}{d x}(\sin x+\cos x+2)+c\Rightarrow 3 \sin x+5 \cos x+4=(A-B) \sin x+(A+B) \cos x+(2 A+C)$
On comparing, we get $A-B=3, A+B=5$ and $2 A+C=4$
So, $A=4, B=1$ and $C=-4\therefore I=\int 4 d x+\int \frac{\frac{d}{d x}(\sin x+\cos x+2)}{(\sin x+\cos x+2)} d x-4 \int \frac{d x}{\sin x+\cos x+2}=4 x+\log (\sin x+\cos x+2)-4 \int \frac{\sec ^2 \frac{x}{2}}{2 \tan \frac{x}{2}+1-\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}+2\left(1+\tan \frac{x}{2}\right)}=4 x+\log (\sin x+\cos x+2)-4 \int \frac{\sec ^2 \frac{x}{2}}{\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}+2 \tan \frac{x}{2}+3} d x=4 x+\log (\sin x+\cos x+2)-4 \int \frac{\sec ^2 \frac{x}{2}}{\left(\tan \frac{x}{2}+1\right)^2+2} d x=4 x+\log (\sin x+\cos x+2)-4 \sqrt{2} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\tan \frac{x}{2}+1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)+c$
Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.q: If $\int e^{\alpha x}\left(\frac{1-\beta \sin x}{1-\cos x}\right) d x=-e^x \cot \frac{x}{2}+c$, then $\frac{\alpha^2+\beta^2}{2 \alpha \beta}=$
questions.solution:
We have,

$\int$e^{$\alpha$x}$\left(\frac{1-\beta \sin x}{1-\cos x}\right)$d x=-e^x \cot $\frac{x}{2}+$c

On differentiating by both sides, we get

e^{$\alpha$x}$\left(\frac{1-\beta \sin x}{1-\cos x}\right)=-$e^x$\left[\cot \frac{x}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \operatorname{cosec}^$2 $\frac{x}{2}\right]

\begin{aligned}$& =-e^x$\left(\frac{\cos \frac{x}{2}}{\sin \frac{x}{2}}-\frac{1}{2 \sin ^2 \frac{x}{2}}\right)=-$e^x$\left[\frac{2 \sin \frac{x}{2} \cos \frac{x}{2}-1}{2 \sin ^2 \frac{x}{2}}\right]$\\
& \Rightarrow \quad e^{$\alpha$x}$\left(\frac{1-\beta \sin x}{1-\cos x}\right)=$e^x$\left(\frac{1-\sin x}{1-\cos x}\right)$\\
& \therefore \quad $\alpha=$1, $\beta=$1
\end{aligned}

Hence,

$\frac{\alpha^2+\beta^2}{2 \alpha \beta}=\frac{1+1}{2}=$1

questions.q: If $\frac{2 x+1}{(x-1)^2\left(x^2+1\right)}=\frac{A}{x-1}+\frac{B}{(x-1)^2}+\frac{C x+D}{x^2+1}$, then $A+B+C+D=$
questions.solution:
1=A(x-1)\left(x^2+1\right)+B\left(x^2+1\right)+(C x+D)(x-1)^2\Rightarrow \quad 2 x+1=x^3(A+C)+x^2(-A+B-2 C+D)+x(A+C-2 D)+(-A+B+D)$
On comparing coefficients of $x^3, x^2, x$ and constant terms both sides we get.
A+C=0\ldots($\mathrm{i}$)-A+B-2 C+D=0\ldots($\mathrm{ii}$)A+C-2 D=2\ldots($\mathrm{iii}$)$
and $\quad-A+B+D=1\ldots($\mathrm{iv}$)$
On solving Eqs. (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv), we get
A=\frac{-1}{2}, B=\frac{3}{2}, C=\frac{1}{2} \text{ and } D=-1\therefore \quad A+B+C+D=\frac{-1}{2}+\frac{3}{2}+\frac{1}{2}-1=\frac{1}{2}$

questions.q: $\int \frac{d x}{\left(2 a x+x^2\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}=$
questions.solution:
We have, $\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{1}{\left(2 a x+x^2\right)^{3 / 2}} d x=\int \frac{1}{x^3\left(\frac{2 a}{x}+1\right)^{3 / 2}} d x \\
& \text{ Put } \begin{aligned}
\frac{2 a}{x}+1 & =t \Rightarrow x=\frac{2 a}{t-1} \Rightarrow \frac{-2 a}{x^2} d x=d t \\
& =-\frac{1}{2 a} \int \frac{t-1}{2 a(t)^{3 / 2}} d t=-\frac{1}{4 a^2} \int \frac{t-1}{t^{3 / 2}} d t
\end{aligned}
\end{aligned} \begin{aligned}& =-\frac{1}{4 a^2} \int\left( t^{-1 / 2}-t^{-3 / 2}\right) d t=-\frac{1}{4 a^2}\left[2 t^{1 / 2}+2 t^{-1 / 2}\right]+c \\
& =-\frac{1}{2 a^2}\left( t^{1 / 2}+t^{-1 / 2}\right)+c=-\frac{1}{2 a^2}\left(\frac{t+1}{\sqrt{t}}\right)+ c
\end{aligned} Put $ t=$\frac{2 a}{x}+1 \begin{aligned}& =-\frac{1}{2 a^2}\left(\frac{\frac{2 a}{x}+1+1}{\sqrt{\frac{2 a}{x}+1}}\right)+ c=-\frac{1}{a^2}\left(\frac{\frac{a}{x}+1}{\sqrt{\frac{2 a}{x}+1}}\right)+ c \\
& =-\frac{1}{a^2}\left(\frac{\frac{a+x}{x}}{\sqrt{\frac{2 a+x}{x}}}\right)+ c=-\frac{1}{a^2}\left(\frac{a+x}{\sqrt{2 a x+x^2}}\right)+ c
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $\int(\sqrt{\tan x}+\sqrt{\cot x}) d x=$
questions.solution:
We have, $\begin{aligned}& \int(\sqrt{\tan x}+\sqrt{\cot x})d x \\
& =\int \left(\sqrt{\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}}+\sqrt{\frac{\cos x}{\sin x}}\right)d x=\int \frac{\sin x+\cos x}{\sqrt{\sin x \cos x}}
\end{aligned} multiply$ and $divide by \sqrt{2}, \begin{aligned}& \quad \sqrt{2} \int \frac{\sin x+\cos x}{\sqrt{2 \sin x \cos x}}d x=\sqrt{2} \int \frac{\sin x+\cos x}{\sqrt{1-1+2 \sin x \cos x}}d x \\
& =\sqrt{2} \int \frac{\sin x+\cos x}{1-(1-2 \sin x \cos x)}d x \\
& =\sqrt{2} \int \frac{\sin x+\cos x}{1-\left(\sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x-2 \sin x \cos x\right)}d x \\
& =\sqrt{2} \int \frac{\sin x+\cos x}{1-(\sin x-\cos x)^2}d x \\
& \text{ Put }(\sinx-\cosx)=t \Rightarrow \quad(\cos x+\sin x) d x=d t \\
& =\sqrt{2} \int \frac{d t}{1-t²}=\sqrt{2} \sin ^^^{-1}t=\sqrt{2} \sin ^{-1}(\sinx-\cosx)+c
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $∫ \sin^{-1}\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{a + x}}dx =$
questions.solution:
We have, $I = ∫ \sin^{-1}\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{a + x}}dx$

Put, $x = a\tan^{2}\theta ⇒ dx = 2atan\theta\sec^{2}\thetad\theta$

$⇒ I = ∫ \sin^{-1}\left(sin\theta\right) \cdot 2atan\theta\sec^{2}\thetad\theta$

Using by parts considering $\theta$ as the first function, we get,

$⇒ I = \left(x + a\right)\tan^{-1}\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{a}} - \sqrt{ax} + c$

questions.q: If $f\left(\frac{t+1}{2 t+1}\right)=t+1$, then $\int f(x) d x=$
questions.solution:
We have, $f\left(\frac{t+1}{2 t+1}\right)=t+1 \begin{aligned}& \text{ Put } \frac{t+1}{2 t+1}= x \Rightarrow t+1=2 t x+x \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 1-x=t(2 x-1) \Rightarrow t=\frac{1-x}{2 x-1}\\
& \therefore \quad f(x)=\frac{1-x}{2 x-1}+1 \Rightarrow f(x)=\frac{1-x+2 x-1}{2 x-1}\\
& \Rightarrow \quad f(x)=\frac{x}{2 x-1}\\
& \therefore \quad \int f(x) d x=\int \frac{x}{2 x-1} d x=\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{2 x}{2 x-1} d x \\
& =\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{2 x-1+1}{2 x-1} d x=\frac{1}{2} \int \lleft(1+\frac{1}{2 x-1}\right) d x \\
& =\frac{1}{2}\l lleft[x+\frac{1}{2} \log(2 x-1)\right]+c \\
& =\frac{x}{2}+\frac{1}{4} \log (2 x-1)+c \\ \text{$ and $} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\int \frac{2 d x}{\sqrt{\cot ^2 x-\tan ^2 x}}=-\sqrt{f(x)}+c$, then $f(x)=$

& =\int \frac{2 \sin x \cos x}{\sqrt{\cos ^4 x-\sin ^4 x}}d x \quad[\because \sin 2 x=2 \sin x \cos x] \\
& =\int \frac{\sin 2 x d x}{\sqrt{\left(\cos ^2 x-\sin ^2 x\right)\left(\cos ^2 x+\sin ^2 x\right)}}\\
& \quad\left[\because \sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x=1 \operatorname{and }^2 x-\sin ^2 x=\cos 2 x\right] \\
& =\int \frac{\sin 2 x d x}{\sqrt{\cos 2 x}}\\
& \text{ Put } \cos2 x=t \quad \Rightarrow \quad-2 \sin 2 x d x=d t \\
& \Rightarrow-\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{d t}{\sqrt{t}}=-\frac{1}{2} \frac{t^{\frac{-1}{2}}+1}{-\frac{1}{2}+1}+c \Rightarrow-\frac{1}{2} \frac{t^{1 / 2}}{\frac{1}{2}}+c=-\sqrt{t}+c \\
& \quad=-\sqrt{\cos 2 x}+c
\end{aligned}

$[t=$\cos 2$ x] \begin{gathered}
=- \sqrt{$\cos 2$ x}+$c \\
\text{ Compare$ with $}-\sqrt{f(x)}+$ c
\end{gathered}

So, $ f(x)=\cos 2 x$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $∫ \dfrac{x}{\left(x^{2} + 1\right)\left(x - 1\right)}dx = Alog\left|x^{2} + 1\right| + B\tan^{-1}x + Clog\left|x - 1\right| + d$, then $A + B + C =$
questions.solution:
Let, $I = ∫ \dfrac{x}{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)\left(x - 1\right)}dx$

By using integration by partial fraction method, we get

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)\left(x - 1\right)} = \dfrac{P}{\left(x - 1\right)} + \dfrac{Qx + R}{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)}$

or $x = P\left({x}^{2} + 1\right) + \left(Qx + R\right)\left(x - 1\right)$

or $x = \left(P + Q\right){x}^{2} + \left(R - Q\right)x + \left(P - R\right)$

By comparing the coefficients, we get

$P + Q = 0 . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

$R - Q = 1 . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

$P - R = 0 . . . . . . \left(3\right)$

On solving the above three equations, we get

$P = \dfrac{1}{2}, Q = - \dfrac{1}{2}, R = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{x}{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)\left(x - 1\right)}dx = ∫ \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}}{\left(x - 1\right)}dx + ∫ \dfrac{- \dfrac{1}{2}x + \dfrac{1}{2}}{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)}dx$

or $I = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{1}{\left(x - 1\right)}dx - \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{x}{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)}dx + \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{1}{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)}dx$

Let ${I}_{1} = - \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{x}{\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)}dx$

Here we take $\left({x}^{2} + 1\right) = t$, then $xdx = \dfrac{dt}{2}$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = - \dfrac{1}{4} ∫ \dfrac{1}{t}dt$

or ${I}_{1} = - \dfrac{1}{4}log\left|t\right|$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}log\left|x - 1\right| - \dfrac{1}{4}log\left|{x}^{2} + 1\right| + \dfrac{1}{2}{tan}^{- 1}x + c$

$⇒ A = - \dfrac{1}{4}, B = \dfrac{1}{2}, C = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Thus, $A + B + C = \dfrac{3}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int e^{2 x} f^{\prime}(x) d x=g(x)$, then $\int\left(e^{2 x} f(x)+e^{2 x} f^{\prime}(x)\right] d x=$

We have, $\begin{aligned}& \int e^{2 x} f^{\prime}(x) d x=g(x) \\

\end{aligned}
$

$\begin{aligned}\int \frac{d x}{x\left(x^4+1\right)}& =\int \frac{x^4+1-x^4}{x\left(x^4+1\right)}d x \\

\begin{aligned}

& =\log|x|-\frac{1}{4} \log |t|+C \\
& =\log|x|-\frac{1}{4} \log \left|x^4+1\right|+C \\
& =\frac{1}{4} \log \left|x^4\right|-\frac{1}{4} \log \left|x^4+1\right|+C \\
& =\frac{1}{4}\left[\log \left|x^4\right|-\log\left|x^4+1\right|\right]+C \\

\end{aligned}
$

questions.q: On $I \subset R-\{-1,1\}, \int \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x}{1-x^2}\right) d x=$
questions.solution:
Let $I_1=\int \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x}{1-x^2}\right) d x$, where

x \in I \subset R-\{-1,1\}

Let us take$ the interval I=(-1,1) \subset R-\{-1,1\}$.
Then, we have

$\begin{gathered}
\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x}{1-x^2}\right)=2 \tan ^{-1} x \\
\therefore I_1=\int2 \tan ^{-1} x d x, \text{ where }$ x \in I=(-1,1) \\
=2 \int_{$\mathrm{II}$ } $\tan _{\mathrm{I}}^{-1}$ x d x
\end{gathered}

Now, by using integration by parts, we get.

\begin{aligned}$ I_1 & =2\left[\tan ^{-1}$ x $\cdot$ x-$\int \frac{1}{1+x²} \cdot$ x d x\right] \\
& =2 x \tan ^{-1} x-$\int \frac{2 x}{1+x²}$ d x \\
& =2 x $\tan ^{-1} x-\log \left(1+x²\right)+C \\
& \quad\left[\because \int \frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{f(x)}$ d x=$\log f$(x)+C\right] \\
& =x $\cdot \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x}{1-x²}\right)-\log \left(1+x²\right)+C
\end{aligned}

\left[\because2 \tan ^{-1} x=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x}{1-x²}\right), \text{$ for }| x| < 1\right]

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int e^{-x} \tan ^{-1}\left(e^x\right) d x=f(x)-\frac{1}{2} \log \left(1+e^{2 x}\right)+C$, then $f(x)$ equals
questions.solution:
Let $I=\int e^{-x} \tan ^{-1}\left(e^x\right) d x$
Put $e^x=t \begin{aligned}& \Rightarrow \quad e^x d x=d t \\
& \Rightarrow \quad d x=\frac{1}{e^x} d t \Rightarrow d x=\frac{1}{t} d t
\end{aligned}

\begin{gathered}
\therefore \quad$ I=$\int \frac{\tan ^{-1} t}{t^2}$ d t \\
=-$\frac{1}{t} \tan ^{-1}$ t-$\int \frac{-1}{t} \cdot \frac{1}{1+t^2}$ d t
\end{gathered}

[using integration by parts]

$\begin{aligned}& =\frac{-1}{t} \tan ^{-1}t+\int \left(\frac{1}{t}-\frac{t}{1+t²}\right)d t \\
& =\frac{-1}{t} \tan ^{-1} t+\log  t-\frac{1}{2} \log \left( 1+t²\right)+C \\
& =-e^{-x} \tan ^{-1}\left( e^x\right)+\log\left( e^x\ \right)-\frac{1}{2} \log \left(1+e^{2 x}\right)+C \\
\therefore & f(x)=-e^{-x} \tan ^{-1}\left(e^x\right)+x=x-e^{-x} \tan ^{-1}\left(e^x\right)
\end{aligned}
$

questions.q: If $\int \frac{x^4+1}{x^6+1} d x=A \tan ^{-1} x+B \tan ^{-1} x^3+c$, then $(A, B)=$
questions.solution:
We have,

$\int \frac{x^4+1}{x^6+1}$d x=A \tan ^{-1} x+B \tan ^{-1} x³+c

Let $I=\int \frac{x^4+1}{x^6+1} d x=\int \frac{x^4+1+x^2-x^2}{\left(x^2\right)^3+(1)^3} d x \begin{aligned}
=$& $\int \frac{\left(x^4-x^2+1\right)+x^2}{\left(x^4+1\right)\left(x^4+1-x^2\right)}$d x \\
& {$\left[\because$a^3+b³=(a+b) $\left(a^2+b²-a b\right)$\right] } \\
= & $\int \frac{d x}{x^2+1}+\int \frac{x^2}{\left(x^2+1\right)\left(x^4+1-x^2\right)}$d x \\
= & $\int \frac{d x}{x^2+1}+\int \frac{x^2}{x^6+1}$d x \\
= & \tan ^{-1} x+$\int \frac{x^2}{\left(x^3\right)^2+1}$d x
\end{aligned}

Put $x^3=t \begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \quad$3 x² d x & =d t \Rightarrow x² d x=$\frac{1}{3}$d t \\
\therefore \quad \quad \quad & =\tan ^{-1} x+$\frac{1}{3} \int \frac{d t}{t^2+1}$\\
& =\tan ^{-2} x+$\frac{1}{3} \tan ^{-1}($t)+c \\
& =\tan ^{-2} x+$\frac{1}{3} \tan ^{-1}\left(x^3\right)+c
\end{aligned}

On comparing it$ with Eq.(i), we getA=1 and B=$\frac{1}{3}.$

questions.q: For any integer $n \geq 2$, let $I_n=\int \tan ^n x d x$. If $I_n=\frac{1}{a} \tan ^{n-1} x-b I_{n-2}$ for $n \geq 2$, then the ordered pair $(a, b)$ equals to
questions.solution:
Given, $I_n=\int \tan ^n x d x \begin{aligned}& =\int \tan ^{n-2} x \cdot \tan ^2 x d x \\
& =\int \tan ^{n-2}\left(\sec ^2 x-1\right) d x \\
& =\int \tan ^{n-2} \sec ^2 x d x-\int \tan ^{n-2} d x \\
& =\frac{\tan ^{n-1}}{n-1}- I_{n-2} \\
& \quad\left[$\begin{array}{l}
\because $\text{ put tan }$ x=t \Rightarrow \sec ^2 x d x=d t \\
$\left.\therefore \int \tan ^{n-2} d t=\frac{t^{n-1}}{n-1}=\frac{$\tan x^{n-1}}{n-1}\right$]$

\end{aligned}$ But it is given $\begin{aligned}& I_n=\frac{1}{a} \tan ^{n-1}- b I_{n-2} \\
\therefore & \quad \frac{1}{a}=\frac{1}{n-1} \text{$ and $} b=1 \\
\Rightarrow \quad & a=n-1, b=1 \\
\therefore \quad & (a, b)=(n-1,1)
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\int \frac{\left(x^2-1\right)}{(x+1)^2 \sqrt{x\left(x^2+x+1\right)}} d x=A \tan ^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\frac{x^2+x+1}{x}}\right)+C$, in which $C$ is a constant, then $A$ equals to
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text{ Let } I=\int \frac{x^2-1}{(x+1)^2 \sqrt{x\left(x^2+x+1\right)}} d x \\ & \text{ Now, } \frac{d}{d x}\left(\tan ^{-1} \sqrt{\frac{x^2+x+1}{x}}\right) \\ & =\frac{1}{1+\frac{x^2+x+1}{x}} \times \frac{d}{d x}\left(\sqrt{\frac{x^2+x+1}{x}}\right) \\ & =\frac{x}{x^2+2 x+1}\left[\frac{\sqrt{x} \times \frac{2 x+1}{2 \sqrt{x^2+x+1}}-\sqrt{x^2+x+1} \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x}}}{(\sqrt{x})^2}\right] \\ & =\frac{x}{x^2+2 x+1}\left[\frac{\sqrt{x}(2 x+1)}{2 \sqrt{\left(x^2+x+1\right)}}-\frac{\sqrt{x^2+x+1}}{2 \sqrt{x}}\right] \\ & =\frac{x}{\left(x^2+2 x+1\right)}\left[\frac{(2 x+1) x-\left(x^2+x+1\right)}{\frac{2 \sqrt{x\left(x^2+x+1\right)}}{x}}\right] \\ & =\frac{x}{(x+1)^2}\left[\frac{x^2-1}{2 x \sqrt{x\left(x^2+x+1\right)}}\right] \\ & =\frac{x^2-1}{2(x+1)^2 \sqrt{x\left(x^2+x+1\right)}} \\ & \end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \therefore I & =\int \frac{d}{d x}\left(2 \tan ^{-1} \sqrt{\frac{x^2+x+1}{x}}\right) \\ & =2 \tan ^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\frac{x^2+x+1}{x}}\right)+C \\ \therefore A & =2\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: $Let \begin{aligned} I & =\int e^x\left(\frac{2+\sin 2 x}{1+\cos 2 x}\right) d x \\ & =\int e^x\left\{\frac{2}{1+\cos 2 x}+\frac{\sin 2 x}{1+\cos 2 x}\right\} d x \\ & =\int e^x\left\{\frac{2}{2 \cos ^2 x}+\frac{2 \sin x \cos x}{2 \cos ^2 x}\right\} d x \\ & =\int e^x\left(\sec ^2 x+\tan x\right) d x \\ & =\int e^x \sec ^2 x d x+\int e^x \tan x d x \\ & =e^x \tan x-\int e^x \tan x d x+\int e^x \tan x d x \\ & =e^x \tan x+C\end{aligned}$

then $p$ is equal to

but given, $\int \frac{x-\sin x}{1+\cos x}$ d x=x \tan $\frac{x}{2}+$ p $\log\left|\sec \frac{x}{2}\right|+$ C On comparing, we get p=-4

questions.q: If $\int \sec ^2 x \operatorname{cosec}^4 x d x=-\frac{1}{3} \cot ^3 x+k \tan x-2 \cot x+C$, then $k$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $I=\int \sec ^2 x \operatorname{cosec}^4 x d x\begin{aligned} & =\int \frac{1}{\sin ^4 x \cos ^2 x} d x=\int \frac{\sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x}{\sin ^4 x \cos ^2 x} d x \\ & =\int \frac{d x}{\sin ^2 x \cos ^2 x}+\int \frac{d x}{\sin ^4 x} \\ & \left.=\int \frac{\left(\sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x\right) d x}{\sin ^2 x \cos ^2 x}+\int \operatorname{cosec}^2 x\right) \\ & =\int\left(\sec ^2 x+\operatorname{cosec}^2 x\right) d x \\ & \quad+\int \operatorname{cosec}^2 x\left(1+\sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x\right) \\ & =\tan x-\cot x+\int \operatorname{cosec}{ }^2 x d x \\ & =\tan x-\cot x-\cot x-\frac{\cot ^3 x}{3}+C \\ & =-\frac{1}{3} \cot ^3 x+\tan x-2 \cot ^2 x+C \cot ^2 x d x\end{aligned}$
But it given that,
$\begin{aligned} & I=-\frac{1}{3} \cot ^3 x+k \tan x-2 \cot x+C \\ \therefore \quad k & =1\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text{ Let } I=\int\left(\sqrt{\frac{a+x}{a-x}}+\sqrt{\frac{a-x}{a+x}}\right) d x \\ & \text{ Put } x=a \cos 2 \theta \Rightarrow d x=-2 a \sin 2 \theta d \theta \\ & \therefore I=-\int\left(\sqrt{\frac{a+a \cos 2 \theta}{a-a \cos 2 \theta}}+\sqrt{\frac{a-a \cos 2 \theta}{a+a \cos 2 \theta}}\right) \\ & \qquad \times 2 a \sin 2 \theta d \theta\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =-\int\left(\sqrt{\frac{2 \cos ^2 \theta}{2 \sin ^2 \theta}}+\sqrt{\frac{2 \sin ^2 \theta}{2 \cos ^2 \theta}}\right) 2 a \sin 2 \theta d \theta \\ & =-2 a \int\left(\frac{\cos \theta}{\sin \theta}+\frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}\right) \sin 2 \theta d \theta \\ & =-2 a \int \frac{1}{\sin \theta \cos \theta} \sin 2 \theta d \theta \\ & =-4 a \int d \theta=-4 a \theta+C_1 \\ & =-2 a \cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{a}\right)+C_1 \\ & =-2 a\left[\frac{\pi}{2}-\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{a}\right)\right]+C_1 \\ & =2 a \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{a}\right)+C_1-\pi a \\ & =2 a \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{a}\right)+C, \text{ where } C=C_1-\pi a\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
If $f_n(x)=\log \log \log \ldots \log x \quad(\log$ is repeated $n$-times), then
$\int\left(x f_1(x) f_2(x) \ldots f_n(x)\right)^{-1} d x$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$f_n(x)=\log \cdot \log \cdot \log \ldots \cdot \log x$ (upto $n$ times)
$f_1(x)=\log xf_2(x)=\log \log xf_3(x)=\log \log \log xf_{n-1}(x)=\log \log \log \ldots \ldots \log x$
(up to $(n-1)$ times)
Now, $\int\left(x f_1(x) f_2(x) \ldots f_n(x)\right)^{-1} d x=\int \frac{d x}{\left[x f_1(x) f_2(x) \ldots f_n(x)\right]}=\int \frac{\left[x f_1(x) f_2(x) \ldots f_{n-1}(x)\right] d t}{\left[x f_1(x) f_2(x) \ldots f_{n-1}(x)\right] \cdot t}=\int \frac{d t}{t}=\log t+c\left[\begin{array}{l}\text{ Put, } f_n(x)=t \\ \frac{d t}{d x}=\frac{1}{\left[f_{n-1}(x) f_{n-2}(x) \ldots f_1(x) \cdot x\right]} \\ d x=\left[x f_1(x) \cdot f_2(x) \ldots f_{n-1}(x)\right] d t\end{array}\right]=\log f_n(x)+c=f_{n+1}(x)+c$
Hence,
$\int\left(x f_1(x) f_2(x) \ldots f_n(x)\right)^{-1} d x=f_{n+1}(x)+c$

questions.q: $\frac{d}{d x}\left[a \tan ^{-1} x+b \log \left(\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right)\right]=\frac{1}{x^4-1}\Rightarrow a-2 b$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, $\frac{d}{d x}\left[a \tan ^{-1} x+b \log \left(\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right)\right]=\frac{1}{x^4-1}$
On integrating both sides, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& a \tan ^{-1} x+b \log \left(\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right) \\
& =\frac{1}{2} \int\left[\frac{1}{x^2-1}-\frac{1}{x^2+1}\right] d x \\
\Rightarrow \quad & a \tan ^{-1} x+b \log \left(\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right) \\
& =\frac{1}{4} \log \left(\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right)-\frac{1}{2} \tan ^{-1} x \\
\Rightarrow \quad & a=-\frac{1}{2}, \quad b=\frac{1}{4} \\
\therefore \quad & a-2 b=-\frac{1}{2}-2\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)=-1
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\int \frac{x+5}{x^2+4 x+5} d x=a \log \left(x^2+4 x+5\right)+b \tan ^{-1}(x+k)+C$, then $(a, b, k)$ equals
questions.solution:
Let $I=\int \frac{x+5}{x^2+4 x+5} d x$
Put $x+5=\lambda(2 x+4)+\mu$
On comparing both sides, we get $\begin{aligned}& \Rightarrow \lambda=2 \lambda \text{$ and $}5=4 \lambda+\mu \\
& \therefore \quad=\frac{1}{2} \text{ and } \mu=3 \\
&=\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{2 x+4}{x^2+4 x+5} d x+3 \int \frac{d x}{x^2+4 x+5}\\
&=\frac{1}{2} \log \left( x^2+4 x+5\right)+3 \int \frac{d x}{(x+2)^2+(1)^2}\\
&=\frac{1}{2} \log \left( x^2+4 x+5\right)+3 \tan ^{-1}(x+2)+C \\

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Observe the following statements :
$\mathrm{A}: \int\left(\frac{x^2-1}{x^2}\right) e^{\frac{x^2+1}{x}} d x=e^{\frac{x^2+1}{x}}+c\mathrm{R}: \int f^{\prime}(x) e^{f(x)} d x=f(x)+c$
Then which of the following is true ?
options: Both A and R are true and R is not the correct reason for $\mathrm{A}$
Both A and R are true and R is the correct reason for $A$
questions.solution:
(A) Let $I=\int\left(\frac{x^2-1}{x^2}\right) e^{\left(\frac{x^2+1}{x}\right)} d x=\int\left(1-\frac{1}{x^2}\right) e^{\left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right)} d x$
Let $\quad x+\frac{1}{x}=t\Rightarrow \quad\left(1-\frac{1}{x^2}\right) d x=d t\therefore \quad I=\int e^t d t=e^t+c=e^{x+\frac{1}{x}}+c=e^{\frac{x^2+1}{x}}+c$
(R) Let $I=\int f^{\prime}(x) e^{f(x)} d x$
Let $f(x)=tf^{\prime}(x) d x=d t\therefore \quad I=\int e^t d t=e^t+c=e^{f(x)}+c$
Thus $A$ is true but $R$ is false.

\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \text{ But } I=\int(x)+c \\
& \therefore \quad \log \left(\frac{\cos x+1}{\cos x}\right)+c=f(x)+c \\

\end{aligned}$
